docs.title: create_tutorial_flow()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_tutorial_flow() -> Flow:

Description: Instantiates all pipeline processing nodes, configures resilience parameters (retries and backoff intervals) for network- and LLM-bound nodes, constructs the execution graph via PocketFlow edge operators, emits a debug trace, and returns an initialized Flow instance with FetchRepo designated as the root entry point.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * Flow: An initialized PocketFlow execution graph instance rooted at the FetchRepo entry node, ready for execution via .run(shared).

Raises: * This factory function does not explicitly raise custom exceptions during graph compilation; however, syntax or structural errors in node connectivity (such as unregistered action branches or invalid edge assignments) will cause pocketflow to raise internal graph validation exceptions during graph construction or execution traversal.

docs.title: Phase 1: Node Allocation and Resilience Configuration
docs.text:
The initialization phase instantiates ten discrete node objects from nodes.py. Nodes that issue external network requests or perform LLM inference are defensively configured with retry limits and exponential backoff timings:

    fetch_repo = FetchRepo()
    context_router = ContextRouter()
    map_abstractions = MapAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    identify_abstractions = IdentifyAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    order_chapters = OrderChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)

In this phase, nodes that perform local memory management or disk I/O (FetchRepo, ContextRouter, and CombineTutorial) are instantiated using their default constructor parameters without retry logic. In contrast, all nodes responsible for generating prompt completions or querying remote LLM APIs (MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters, and DeterministicFileMapper) explicitly configure max_retries=5 and wait=20. This configuration ensures that transient network failures, HTTP 429 rate-limiting events, and upstream model service interruptions automatically trigger up to five retry attempts with a twenty-second cooldown interval between iterations before aborting the entire pipeline execution.

docs.title: Phase 2: Ingestion and Dynamic Branch Routing
docs.text:
The second phase connects the repository ingestion stage to the context evaluation router and defines the three-way operational branching logic:

    fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper

The linear edge operator fetch_repo >> context_router establishes that once repository discovery, cloning, or local walking finishes, the shared pipeline state transitions immediately to ContextRouter. The router evaluates codebase token density against model context limits, triggering one of three conditional edges using PocketFlow's action-binding syntax (context_router - "<action>" >> <target_node>): - When ContextRouter.prep() or .exec() emits "direct", the execution engine transitions to IdentifyAbstractions, initiating single-pass architectural extraction. - When it emits "batch", execution diverts to MapAbstractions to chunk and distribute codebase analysis across multiple parallel or sequential LLM context windows. - When it emits "deterministic", the pipeline activates DeterministicFileMapper, bypassing LLM abstraction discovery entirely in favor of an explicit one-to-one file-to-chapter structural mapping.

docs.title: Phase 3: Abstraction Mapping and Linear Consolidation
docs.text:
The third phase handles the convergence of abstraction discovery into relationship mapping and chapter ordering:

    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters

Under the "batch" branch, MapAbstractions passes its chunked intermediate abstractions directly into ReduceAbstractions (map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions), which consolidates duplicate concepts, reconciles naming variances, and synthesizes a unified list of high-level architectural abstractions. The outputs of both IdentifyAbstractions (from the "direct" branch) and ReduceAbstractions (from the "batch" branch) feed into AnalyzeRelationships. This node constructs an architectural dependency matrix between the identified systems. Once dependencies are mapped, analyze_relationships >> order_chapters transitions state to OrderChapters, which performs topological and narrative sorting to organize the documentation sequence before passing control to WriteChapters.

docs.title: Phase 4: Deterministic Bypass and Final Compilation
docs.text:
The final phase wires the deterministic fast-path into the chapter writing node, terminates the workflow with tutorial assembly, emits diagnostic logging, and returns the assembled graph:

    deterministic_mapper >> write_chapters

    write_chapters >> combine_tutorial

    emit_raw("DEBUG", "create_tutorial_flow | constructed PocketFlow execution graph", dest="LOG")
    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

The deterministic fast-path bypasses AnalyzeRelationships and OrderChapters, linking DeterministicFileMapper directly to WriteChapters (deterministic_mapper >> write_chapters). Because DeterministicFileMapper precomputes explicit chapter targets and structural ordering directly from file paths, intermediate abstraction modeling is unnecessary. Both the abstraction analysis track and the deterministic track converge at WriteChapters, which generates the Markdown documentation content for each chapter. The completed chapters flow into CombineTutorial (write_chapters >> combine_tutorial) for final cross-linking, navigation manifest assembly, and MkDocs site compilation. Once the graph is fully declared, emit_raw() logs a diagnostic trace to the internal log file via utils/output.py, and the graph is returned encapsulated within a Flow instance rooted at fetch_repo.

Example: 

# Extracted from flow.py: Full graph construction and execution initialization
from flow import create_tutorial_flow

# Instantiate the pipeline graph
tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()

# Execute graph traversal with a shared context dictionary (as called in main.py)
# shared_state = {"repo_path": "/path/to/repo", "language": "en"}
# tutorial_flow.run(shared_state)

docs.title: Internal Helpers
docs.text: The flow.py module defines no internal helper functions or private module-level classes. All node instantiation, parameter configuration, edge routing, and graph assembly operations are contained entirely within the public factory function create_tutorial_flow().

docs.title: Graph Node Routing Contract
docs.text:
While flow.py does not define new classes, it creates and configures the node connectivity matrix for the pocketflow.Flow engine. The following table details each node instantiated within create_tutorial_flow(), its operational responsibilities, its inbound/outbound edge bindings, and its retry configuration:

Node Variable Class Type Inbound Predecessor(s) Outbound Action / Condition Outbound Successor(s) Configured Retry Parameters fetch_repo FetchRepo Root / Entry Point Default (None) context_router Default (max_retries=0, wait=0) context_router ContextRouter fetch_repo "direct""batch""deterministic" identify_abstractionsmap_abstractionsdeterministic_mapper Default (max_retries=0, wait=0) identify_abstractions IdentifyAbstractions context_router ("direct") Default (None) analyze_relationships max_retries=5, wait=20 map_abstractions MapAbstractions context_router ("batch") Default (None) reduce_abstractions max_retries=5, wait=20 reduce_abstractions ReduceAbstractions map_abstractions Default (None) analyze_relationships max_retries=5, wait=20 deterministic_mapper DeterministicFileMapper context_router ("deterministic") Default (None) write_chapters max_retries=5, wait=20 analyze_relationships AnalyzeRelationships identify_abstractionsreduce_abstractions Default (None) order_chapters max_retries=5, wait=20 order_chapters OrderChapters analyze_relationships Default (None) write_chapters max_retries=5, wait=20 write_chapters WriteChapters order_chaptersdeterministic_mapper Default (None) combine_tutorial max_retries=5, wait=20 combine_tutorial CombineTutorial write_chapters Terminal Node None (Execution Terminates) Default (max_retries=0, wait=0)

docs.title: Action Branching Schema
docs.text:
ContextRouter conditionally dictates pipeline progression through explicit string action tokens:

Action Identifier Target Node Selection Criterion "direct" IdentifyAbstractions Codebase files and structural summaries fit completely within the active LLM context window without chunking. "batch" MapAbstractions Codebase size exceeds single-prompt context thresholds, requiring a Map-Reduce partitioning strategy. "deterministic" DeterministicFileMapper The user or system selects explicit 1:1 file-to-chapter mapping (e.g., in advanced mode or for flat reference documentation), skipping abstraction discovery.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Error handling in flow.py is configured declaratively across node definitions and framework-level execution primitives:

  • Transient LLM and Network Failures: Nodes interfacing with remote APIs (MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters, and DeterministicFileMapper) are initialized with max_retries=5 and wait=20. If an underlying call within utils/call_llm.py fails due to rate limits (HTTP 429), gateway timeouts (HTTP 504), or malformed response serialization, PocketFlow intercepts the failure, sleeps for twenty seconds, and retries up to five times before allowing the exception to propagate to main.py.
  • Graph Traversal Integrity: In PocketFlow, edges defined with conditional actions (- "action" >> target) must match the string returned by the source node's .post() method. If ContextRouter returns an unmapped action string (e.g., an unhandled runtime mode), PocketFlow halts graph execution, preventing undefined states from propagating downstream.
  • Logging Isolation: Graph construction concludes with emit_raw("DEBUG", ..., dest="LOG"). By routing this trace exclusively to the LOG destination, flow.py avoids polluting the console UI while preserving graph initialization diagnostics in llm_cache.json or the active run log file.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• main.py — The application entry point that invokes create_tutorial_flow() and executes .run(shared) on the returned graph.
  • nodes.py — Implements all pipeline processing nodes instantiated and connected within flow.py.
  • utils/call_llm.py — The underlying model inference gateway whose rate limits and error profiles necessitate the max_retries=5, wait=20 configuration.
  • utils/token_utils.py — Context estimation utilities used by ContextRouter to choose between "direct" and "batch" branches.
  • utils/output.py — Telemetry and diagnostic logging module providing emit_raw().

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Building upon the orchestration pipeline defined in flow.py, which coordinates PocketFlow nodes and directs workflow branches across execution modes, main.py serves as the primary executable entry point and CLI orchestration harness for the entire Codebase-Knowledge-Builder application. While flow.py models the abstract computation graph and execution dependencies, main.py grounds this topology in a concrete runtime context by parsing command-line parameters, discovering provider credentials, configuring logging and localization subsystems, and constructing the unified shared state store passed through the graph.

The module encapsulates operational concerns including argument parsing, shell-escaping defect detection, documentation mode resolution, LLM environment introspection, incremental caching integrity checks, and post-execution cleanup routines. By abstracting these CLI and environment configurations, main.py ensures that whether an operator is targeting a remote public GitHub repository or a local filesystem directory, all configuration parameters—such as token budgets, exclusion globs, thinking budgets, and MkDocs site specifications—are normalized into the canonical shape expected by downstream nodes.

The module operates as a deterministic bootstrap pipeline consisting of five distinct operational phases: CLI specification and parsing, quoting error validation, runtime environment and cache constraint resolution, unified shared state store construction, and PocketFlow graph execution. docs.title: parse_arguments()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_arguments() -> tuple[argparse.ArgumentParser, argparse.Namespace]:

Description: Constructs the command-line interface specification using Python's standard argparse module, registering all mutually exclusive source groups, operational mode switches, token limits, exclusion patterns, and debugging parameters. It returns both the instantiated ArgumentParser instance and the resulting parsed Namespace. This dual return allows downstream components, specifically _check_quoting_errors, to inspect configured option strings dynamically directly from the parser actions without maintaining hardcoded flag lists.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * tuple[argparse.ArgumentParser, argparse.Namespace]: A 2-tuple containing the configured argparse.ArgumentParser instance and the populated argparse.Namespace object containing parsed CLI values.

Raises: * SystemExit: Automatically triggered by argparse if unrecognized arguments are passed or if required argument groups fail validation.

docs.title: Phase 1: Parser and Source Group Definition
docs.text:
def parse_arguments():
    """Parse and return command-line arguments."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate a tutorial for a GitHub codebase or local directory.")

    # Source: --repo or --dir (mutually exclusive but not required if --cleanup is used)
    source_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    source_group.add_argument("--repo", help="URL of the public GitHub repository.")
    source_group.add_argument("--dir", help="Path to local directory.")
    parser.add_argument("--cleanup", action="store_true", help="Clean up logs and cache files. Can be used standalone or after a run.")

    parser.add_argument("-n", "--name", help="Project name (optional, derived from repo/directory if omitted).")
    parser.add_argument("-t", "--token", help="GitHub personal access token (optional, reads from GITHUB_TOKEN env var if not provided).")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", default="output", help="Base directory for output (default: ./output).")
    # ...
Phase 1 instantiates the root parser and defines the primary intake coordinates. A mutually exclusive group ensures that the operator cannot supply both a remote repository URL (--repo) and a local filesystem directory path (--dir) within the same invocation. Crucially, neither option is marked as strictly required at the argparse group level; this design permits --cleanup to run as a standalone utility without requiring a dummy codebase target. Default base directory output is anchored to ./output, while the optional project name (-n/--name) and GitHub personal access token (-t/--token) provide overrides for target identification and Git API authentication.

docs.title: Phase 2: Ingestion Filters and Token Limits
docs.text:
# ...
    parser.add_argument("-i", "--include", nargs="+", help="Files to include (e.g., '*.py' '*.js'). Defaults to '*' (all files).")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-e",
        "--exclude",
        nargs="+",
        help="Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("-s", "--max-size", type=int, default=200000, help="Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200000, about 200KB).")
    # Add language parameter for multi-language support
    parser.add_argument("--language", default="english", help="Language for the generated tutorial (default: english).")
    # Add use_cache parameter to control LLM caching
    parser.add_argument("--no-cache", action="store_true", help="Disable LLM response caching (default: caching enabled).")
    # Add max_abstraction_num parameter to control the number of abstractions
    parser.add_argument("--max-abstractions", type=int, default=10, help="Maximum number of abstractions to identify (default: 10).")
    # Add thinking_level parameter for LLM reasoning capabilities
    parser.add_argument(
        "--thinking-level",
        default=None,
        help="Thinking effort level for native Gemini, OpenRouter, and Ollama reasoning models (e.g., low, medium, high). Leave empty to use model defaults.",
    )
    # Add max_tokens parameter
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-tokens", type=int, default=None, help="Maximum number of tokens for the context window (default: fetched dynamically)."
    )
    # ...
Phase 2 registers ingestion filtering flags (--include, --exclude, --max-size), along with LLM synthesis parameters. File patterns support multi-argument sequences via nargs="+", which are later combined with module defaults. Token limits and caching mechanics are declared through --no-cache (which inverts to use_cache=False) and --max-tokens (which bypasses dynamic context window detection). The --thinking-level flag enables operators to modulate reasoning budgets for models supporting native reasoning protocols (such as Gemini 2.0/3.0 or OpenRouter models), while --language establishes the target localization dialect across downstream generation prompts.

docs.title: Phase 3: Mode Selection and Batch Controls
docs.text:
# ...
    # --- Documentation Mode & Generation Styles ---
    parser.add_argument(
        "--mode",
        choices=["tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk"],
        default="tutorial",
        help="Documentation style (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk). (default: tutorial).",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--advanced", action="store_true", help="Legacy flag: equivalent to --mode advanced.")
    parser.add_argument("--mkdocs", action="store_true", help="Format output for MkDocs Material (adds YAML frontmatter & nav snippet).")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--incremental",
        action="store_true",
        help="Enable MD5 incremental caching to skip unchanged modules (Only supported in --mode api-reference).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--force-rebuild", action="store_true", help="Clear incremental cache and regenerate all chapters from scratch (use with --incremental)."
    )

    # Add batching parameters
    parser.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=50, help="Maximum files per batch when using map-reduce mode (default: 50).")
    parser.add_argument("--force-batch", action="store_true", help="Force map-reduce mode regardless of context size.")
    # Debug mode
    parser.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true", help="Enable verbose debug output.")

    return parser, parser.parse_args()
Phase 3 establishes pipeline routing switches and output targets. The --mode flag exposes four distinct documentation styles: tutorial, advanced, api-reference, and sdk. Backward compatibility is preserved via --advanced, which acts as an alias for --mode advanced. MkDocs Material static site structuring is requested via --mkdocs, while --incremental and --force-rebuild control MD5-based incremental generation in API reference workflows. Finally, --batch and --force-batch control map-reduce partitioning behavior inside ContextRouter (nodes.py), and --debug toggles verbose telemetry output across logging channels.

Example: 

# Extracted from main.py entry point
parser, args = parse_arguments()
init_output(
    language=args.language,
    use_cache=not args.no_cache,
    thinking_level=args.thinking_level,
    debug=args.debug,
)

docs.title: resolve_mode_and_project()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_mode_and_project(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, str]:

Description: Normalizes the operational documentation mode and derives the target project name from CLI arguments and environment variables. If the legacy --advanced boolean flag is passed, it forces the mode to "advanced", issuing a warning if the operator simultaneously specified a non-tutorial --mode. If the operator does not supply an explicit project name via -n/--name, the function dynamically computes it by taking the trailing path component of --dir or the final segment of the repository URL --repo.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI command-line options.

Returns: * tuple[str, str]: A 2-tuple containing the resolved documentation mode string (e.g., "tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk") and the resolved project name string.

Raises: * No exceptions raised directly; warnings are emitted via emit("WARN_ADVANCED_OVERRIDES_MODE").

Implementation: 

def resolve_mode_and_project(args):
    """Resolve documentation mode (handling --advanced legacy flag) and derive project name.

    Returns:
        tuple[str, str]: (mode, project_name)
    """
    if args.advanced:
        if args.mode != "tutorial":  # User explicitly set --mode AND --advanced
            emit("WARN_ADVANCED_OVERRIDES_MODE", mode=args.mode)
        mode = "advanced"
    else:
        mode = args.mode
    project_name = args.name
    if not project_name:
        if args.dir:
            project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir))
        elif args.repo:
            project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
        else:
            project_name = "project"
    return mode, project_name
The resolution logic prioritizes explicit legacy flags before falling back to the designated args.mode. For project name resolution, the function normalizes filesystem directories using os.path.abspath() prior to invoking os.path.basename(), preventing empty string names when trailing directory slashes are provided on Unix systems. For remote repositories, trailing slashes are stripped via .rstrip("/") before extracting the final path token. If neither source is configured (for example, during standalone execution), it safely defaults to "project".

Example: 

# Extracted from main.py execution flow
mode, project_name = resolve_mode_and_project(args)

# Enforce incremental cache constraints
if args.incremental and mode != "api-reference":
    emit("WARN_INCREMENTAL_API_ONLY")
    args.incremental = False

docs.title: build_shared_store()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_shared_store(args: argparse.Namespace, github_token: str | None, mode: str) -> dict[str, Any]:

Description: Assembles the central shared state dictionary passed between PocketFlow nodes throughout graph execution. It combines CLI flags, resolved configurations, calculated exclusion sets, and empty output slots (files, abstractions, relationships, chapter_order, chapters) into a single mutable dictionary.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): The parsed CLI arguments namespace. * github_token (str | None): Authenticated GitHub personal access token, if resolved. * mode (str): The resolved documentation mode string.

Returns: * dict[str, Any]: The initialized pipeline data store dictionary containing configuration options, pattern collections, and empty result placeholders.

Raises: * No exceptions raised directly.

Implementation: 

def build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode):
    """Construct the shared store dictionary passed between PocketFlow nodes.

    Returns:
        dict: The shared store with all CLI args, patterns, and empty output slots.
    """
    return {
        "repo_url": args.repo,
        "local_dir": args.dir,
        "project_name": args.name,  # Can be None, FetchRepo will derive it
        "github_token": github_token,
        "output_dir": args.output,  # Base directory for CombineTutorial output
        # Include/exclude patterns and max file size
        "include_patterns": set(args.include) if args.include else DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "exclude_patterns": DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS.union(set(args.exclude)) if args.exclude else DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS,
        "max_file_size": args.max_size,
        # Language for multi-language support
        "language": args.language,
        # Cache flag (inverse of no-cache)
        "use_cache": not args.no_cache,
        # Max abstractions
        "max_abstraction_num": args.max_abstractions,
        # LLM reasoning capabilities
        "thinking_level": args.thinking_level,
        # Max tokens override
        "max_tokens": args.max_tokens,
        # Mode, mkdocs, and incremental
        "mode": mode,
        "mkdocs": args.mkdocs,
        "incremental": args.incremental,
        "advanced_mode": mode == "advanced",
        # Batching settings
        "batch_size": args.batch,
        "force_batch": args.force_batch,
        # Debug mode
        "debug": args.debug,
        # Outputs populated by downstream nodes
        "files": [],
        "abstractions": [],
        "relationships": {},
        "chapter_order": [],
        "chapters": [],
        "final_output_dir": None,
    }
The state constructor handles the union of custom exclude patterns with the global DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS constant imported from utils/exclude_patterns.py. The use_cache boolean is set to the logical inverse of args.no_cache. Crucially, output fields such as files, abstractions, and chapters are initialized as empty lists or dictionaries, providing deterministic mutation targets for FetchRepo, IdentifyAbstractions, OrderChapters, and WriteChapters in nodes.py.

Example: 

# Extracted from main.py execution flow
shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode)
provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)
log_file = configure_logging(project_name=project_name, mode=mode)
display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file)

# Create and run the flow
tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()
tutorial_flow.run(shared)

docs.title: detect_llm_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def detect_llm_config(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[str, str, str, str, int]:

Description: Inspects runtime environment variables to determine the active LLM provider, target model name, API endpoint URL, authentication key, and model context length ceiling. If an explicit provider is declared via LLM_PROVIDER, it pulls provider-prefixed environment variables (such as {provider}_MODEL and {provider}_BASE_URL). If unset, it inspects Gemini-specific environment variables (GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY) as a standard default fallback. When no explicit --max-tokens flag is passed via CLI, it invokes get_model_context_length from utils/call_llm.py to dynamically compute or query the model context ceiling.

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed command-line arguments (used to check args.max_tokens).

Returns: * tuple[str, str, str, str, int]: A 5-tuple consisting of: 1. provider (str): The resolved provider key (e.g., "OPENROUTER", "GEMINI", "UNKNOWN"). 2. model_name (str): The target model identifier string. 3. endpoint_url (str): The API base endpoint URL. 4. api_key (str): The resolved API key string. 5. context_length (int): The maximum context window token limit.

Raises: * No exceptions raised directly. Network or parsing failures during context retrieval degrade to default integer token limits.

Implementation: 

def detect_llm_config(args):
    """Detect LLM provider, model, endpoint, and context length from environment.

    Returns:
        tuple: (provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length)
    """
    from utils.call_llm import get_model_context_length

    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider:
        model_name = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", "unknown")
        endpoint_url = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_BASE_URL", "unknown")
        api_key = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_API_KEY", "")
    else:
        # Fallback to Gemini if neither provider is explicitly set but it's used
        if os.environ.get("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
            provider = "GEMINI"
            model_name = os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")
            endpoint_url = "generativelanguage.googleapis.com"
            api_key = os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
        else:
            provider = "UNKNOWN"
            model_name = "unknown"
            endpoint_url = "unknown"
            api_key = ""

    context_length = args.max_tokens or get_model_context_length(endpoint_url, model_name, api_key)
    return provider, model_name, endpoint_url, api_key, context_length
The helper relies on a late local import (from utils.call_llm import get_model_context_length) to avoid cyclic initialization issues during module load time. When evaluating context_length, args.max_tokens takes absolute precedence; if omitted, the remote model context boundary is evaluated through OpenRouter metadata endpoints or static heuristic tables mapped inside utils/call_llm.py.

Example: 

# Extracted from main.py execution flow
provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)
log_file = configure_logging(project_name=project_name, mode=mode)
display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file)

docs.title: display_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def display_config(args: argparse.Namespace, mode: str, provider: str, model_name: str, endpoint_url: str, context_length: int, log_file: str) -> None:

Description: Formats and outputs the complete operational configuration summary banner to the console before graph execution begins. It formats token boundaries with comma separators, resolves internationalized string representations for enabled/disabled features via get(), and suppresses or adapts output based on documentation modes (e.g., displaying CFG_VALUE_API_REF_MAX when mode == "api-reference").

Parameters: * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI command-line arguments. * mode (str): Resolved documentation mode string. * provider (str): The detected LLM provider string. * model_name (str): The target LLM model name. * endpoint_url (str): The API base endpoint URL. * context_length (int): Token capacity of the LLM context window. * log_file (str): Filesystem path to the active execution run's log file.

Returns: * None: Outputs formatted diagnostics directly to the operational log/console via emit().

Raises: * No exceptions raised directly.

Implementation: 

def display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file):
    """Emit all configuration values to the console."""
    emit("START_GENERATION", source=args.repo or args.dir, language=args.language.capitalize())
    emit("CFG_HEADER")
    emit("CFG_AI_PROVIDER", value=provider)
    emit("CFG_AI_ENDPOINT", value=endpoint_url)
    emit("CFG_AI_MODEL", value=model_name)
    emit("CFG_CONTEXT_LENGTH", value=f"{context_length:,}")
    emit("CFG_THINKING_LEVEL", value=args.thinking_level or "None")
    emit("CFG_BATCH_SIZE", value=f"{args.batch}")
    _enabled = get("CFG_VALUE_ENABLED")
    _disabled = get("CFG_VALUE_DISABLED")
    emit("CFG_FORCE_BATCH", value=_enabled if args.force_batch else _disabled)
    emit("CFG_OUTPUT_MODE", value=mode)
    emit("CFG_MKDOCS", value=_enabled if args.mkdocs else _disabled)
    emit("CFG_INCREMENTAL", value=_enabled if args.incremental else _disabled)
    if args.incremental:
        emit("CFG_FORCE_REBUILD", value=_enabled if args.force_rebuild else _disabled)
    if mode == "api-reference":
        emit("CFG_MAX_ABSTRACTIONS", value=get("CFG_VALUE_API_REF_MAX"))
    else:
        emit("CFG_MAX_ABSTRACTIONS", value=str(args.max_abstractions))
    emit("CFG_LLM_CACHING", value=_disabled if args.no_cache else _enabled)
    if args.debug:
        emit("CFG_DEBUG_MODE")
    emit("CFG_LOG_FILE", value=log_file)
    print()  # Blank line after config block
The routine bridges the CLI parameters with the centralized localization framework in utils/output.py. Rather than printing hardcoded English strings to standard out, it dispatches internationalized tokens (START_GENERATION, CFG_HEADER, CFG_AI_PROVIDER, etc.) through emit(). It dynamically pulls localized representations for boolean statuses (CFG_VALUE_ENABLED vs CFG_VALUE_DISABLED) and accommodates special mode configurations, such as overriding numeric abstraction counts with dynamic indicators in API reference mode.

Example: 

# Extracted from main.py execution flow
shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode)
provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)
log_file = configure_logging(project_name=project_name, mode=mode)
display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file)

docs.title: main()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def main() -> None:

Description: The top-level workflow orchestrator of the application. It parses input flags, validates shell quoting integrity, checks source target prerequisites, handles standalone cache cleanup, normalizes modes, enforces incremental compilation rules, initializes logging, builds the shared dictionary, creates the tutorial flow graph via flow.py, and triggers execution.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * SystemExit: Raised on quoting validation failure, missing source flags, or incompatible incremental rebuild configurations.

docs.title: Phase 1: CLI Intake, Output Initialization, and Quoting Validation
docs.text:
def main():
    parser, args = parse_arguments()
    init_output(
        language=args.language,
        use_cache=not args.no_cache,
        thinking_level=args.thinking_level,
        debug=args.debug,
    )
    _check_quoting_errors(parser, args)

    # Handle standalone --cleanup (no --dir or --repo)
    if args.cleanup and not args.dir and not args.repo:
        _run_cleanup()
        return

    # Require --dir or --repo for generation
    if not args.dir and not args.repo:
        parser.error("one of the arguments --repo --dir --cleanup is required")
    # ...
Phase 1 parses CLI arguments, boots the output rendering system via init_output(), and checks for shell quoting errors using _check_quoting_errors(). It then inspects standalone commands: if --cleanup is invoked without a codebase source (--dir or --repo), it executes _run_cleanup() and terminates immediately without raising an error. If neither a source directory nor a repository is supplied for a generation run, it halts with parser.error().

docs.title: Phase 2: Credentials and Mode Verification
docs.text:
# ...
    # Get GitHub token from argument or environment variable if using repo
    github_token = None
    if args.repo:
        github_token = args.token or os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
        if not github_token:
            emit("WARN_NO_GITHUB_TOKEN")
    elif args.token:
        emit("WARN_TOKEN_NO_REPO")

    mode, project_name = resolve_mode_and_project(args)

    # Enforce incremental cache constraints
    if args.incremental and mode != "api-reference":
        emit("WARN_INCREMENTAL_API_ONLY")
        args.incremental = False

    # --force-rebuild requires --incremental
    if args.force_rebuild and not args.incremental:
        emit("ERROR_FORCE_REBUILD_NO_INCREMENTAL")
        sys.exit(1)
    # ...
Phase 2 resolves authentication credentials and validates mode constraints. For GitHub repository targets, it checks the CLI argument -t/--token before falling back to the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable, emitting a warning if no token is available for remote crawling. It resolves the operational mode and project name, then enforces incremental caching rules: --incremental is deactivated with a warning if used outside api-reference mode, and --force-rebuild triggers an immediate exit if invoked without --incremental.

docs.title: Phase 3: Manifest Purging and State Initialization
docs.text:
# ...
    # Handle --force-rebuild: delete the cache manifest to force fresh generation
    if args.force_rebuild and args.incremental:
        output_base = args.output or "output"
        manifest_path = os.path.join(output_base, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
        if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
            os.remove(manifest_path)
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_DELETED", path=manifest_path)
        else:
            emit("FORCE_REBUILD_NO_MANIFEST", path=manifest_path)

    # Warn about args ignored in api-reference mode

        emit("WARN_FORCE_BATCH_API_REF")

    shared = build_shared_store(args, github_token, mode)
    provider, model_name, endpoint_url, _, context_length = detect_llm_config(args)

    display_config(args, mode, provider, model_name, endpoint_url, context_length, log_file)
    # ...
Phase 3 manages cache invalidation, parameter overrides, and pipeline state initialization. When --force-rebuild is active, it locates and unlinks the .doc_cache_manifest.json file inside the target project output directory. If api-reference mode is selected with --force-batch, it deactivates batching and emits a warning, as API reference generation operates deterministically per module rather than using map-reduce batching. Finally, it constructs the shared dictionary, detects the active LLM configuration, initializes the logging file handler via configure_logging(), and prints the configuration banner.

docs.text:
# ...
    # Create and run the flow
    tutorial_flow = create_tutorial_flow()
    tutorial_flow.run(shared)

    # Cleanup after run if requested
    if args.cleanup:
        _run_cleanup()

Phase 4 instantiates the PocketFlow Directed Acyclic Graph by calling create_tutorial_flow() from flow.py and begins execution by invoking tutorial_flow.run(shared). Once the graph completes execution (writing out tutorials, API documentation, or MkDocs bundles via CombineTutorial in nodes.py), it checks the --cleanup flag. If --cleanup was specified alongside generation arguments, _run_cleanup() purges the persistent response cache and log directories after the run finishes.

docs.title: _check_quoting_errors()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _check_quoting_errors(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser, args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:

Description: Detects shell quoting errors where values passed to multi-argument options (specifically --exclude and --include) accidentally absorb subsequent CLI flags. When an operator misquotes an argument string (such as --exclude "autogen/* "SmartFO/*" --language Vietnamese), Unix shells group all trailing flags into the pattern string, silently ignoring those CLI flags. This function extracts all registered flag options dynamically from parser._actions and checks if any pattern contains an embedded flag string. If a shell quoting error is detected, it emits an ERROR_QUOTING message and exits immediately.

Parameters: * parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The active CLI parser instance, used to dynamically discover registered flags. * args (argparse.Namespace): Parsed CLI arguments containing pattern lists to evaluate.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * SystemExit: Exits with status code 1 if an embedded flag is detected within any pattern string.

Implementation: 

def _check_quoting_errors(parser, args):
    """Detect shell quoting errors where --exclude/--include values accidentally swallowed other CLI flags.

    When users misquote patterns (e.g., --exclude "autogen/* "SmartFO/*" --language Vietnamese),
    the shell merges subsequent flags into the pattern value. This silently causes ALL following
    arguments to be ignored. We detect this by checking if any pattern value contains a known
    CLI flag string, which no legitimate file/directory pattern would ever contain.

    Flags are extracted dynamically from the argparse parser — no hardcoded list to maintain.
    """
    # Extract all registered flags (both --long and -short) from the parser
    known_flags = set()
    for action in parser._actions:
        for opt in action.option_strings:
            known_flags.add(opt)

    for pattern_list, flag_name in [(args.exclude, "--exclude"), (args.include, "--include")]:
        if not pattern_list:
            continue
        for pattern in pattern_list:
            for known_flag in known_flags:
                if f" {known_flag} " in pattern or (f" {known_flag}" in pattern and pattern.endswith(known_flag)):
                    emit(
                        "ERROR_QUOTING",
                        flag=flag_name,
                        pattern=pattern[:120],
                        embedded=known_flag,
                    )
                    sys.exit(1)
The helper inspects all action.option_strings registered across the parser, discovering both short (-o) and long (--output) flags without maintaining a hardcoded list. It evaluates candidate patterns in both args.exclude and args.include. By checking for patterns containing " {flag} " (a flag surrounded by spaces) or ending with " {flag}", it catches swallowed arguments while avoiding false positives on file paths that might contain flag substrings without whitespace boundaries.

Example: 

# Invocation inside main() directly after argument parsing
parser, args = parse_arguments()
init_output(...)
_check_quoting_errors(parser, args)

docs.title: _run_cleanup()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _run_cleanup() -> None:

Description: Cleans up transient cache files and execution logs generated by the application. It deletes the persistent LLM disk cache (llm_cache.json) and removes the logging directory configured in LOG_DIR (defaulting to ./logs) using shutil.rmtree(). Deletion events, directories removed, and filesystem errors are reported via emit().

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * None.

Raises: * No exceptions raised. Filesystem exceptions during deletion are caught and reported via emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", ...).

Implementation: 

def _run_cleanup():
    """Clean up cache files and log directory."""
    import shutil

    emit("CLEANUP_START")

    for cache_path in ["llm_cache.json"]:
        if os.path.exists(cache_path):
            try:
                os.remove(cache_path)
                emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED", path=cache_path)
            except Exception as e:
                emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=cache_path, error=e)

    log_dir = os.environ.get("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    if os.path.exists(log_dir) and os.path.isdir(log_dir):
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(log_dir)
            emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED_DIR", path=log_dir)
        except Exception as e:
            emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=log_dir, error=e)
The cleanup routine uses dynamic scoped imports (import shutil) to manage directory removal without adding unnecessary top-level dependencies. It wraps filesystem deletions in try...except Exception blocks, ensuring that locked files or permission issues do not crash the application or prevent subsequent cleanup steps from executing.

Example: 

# Standalone cleanup path inside main()
if args.cleanup and not args.dir and not args.repo:
    _run_cleanup()
    return

docs.title: Shell Quoting Trap Detection
docs.text:
When operators misquote arguments containing wildcards (for instance, --exclude "vendor/* "src/*"), shells absorb subsequent CLI flags into the pattern string, silently dropping configuration flags. The _check_quoting_errors() function intercepts this by checking patterns against all registered parser options. When a pattern contains an embedded flag token, it aborts immediately: 

if f" {known_flag} " in pattern or (f" {known_flag}" in pattern and pattern.endswith(known_flag)):
    emit(
        "ERROR_QUOTING",
        flag=flag_name,
        pattern=pattern[:120],
        embedded=known_flag,
    )
    sys.exit(1)

docs.title: Mutually Exclusive Sources and Mandatory Intake Validation
docs.text:
main.py uses parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group() to prevent specifying both --repo and --dir in a single run. If neither source is supplied, it checks for standalone --cleanup; if that flag is also absent, it calls parser.error(): 

if not args.dir and not args.repo:
    parser.error("one of the arguments --repo --dir --cleanup is required")

docs.title: Incremental Cache Integrity Rules
docs.text:
To prevent inconsistent build states, main.py enforces constraints around incremental cache flags: 1. --incremental is supported only in api-reference mode. If specified with other modes, it is disabled and a warning is emitted: 

if args.incremental and mode != "api-reference":
    emit("WARN_INCREMENTAL_API_ONLY")
    args.incremental = False
2. --force-rebuild requires --incremental. If used without --incremental, the program emits an error and exits: 
if args.force_rebuild and not args.incremental:
    emit("ERROR_FORCE_REBUILD_NO_INCREMENTAL")
    sys.exit(1)

docs.title: Non-Fatal Cleanup Trapping
docs.text:
Filesystem failures during cache purging or directory removal in _run_cleanup() are caught via except Exception as e and logged using emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", ...). This ensures transient file locks do not crash the application during teardown: 

try:
    shutil.rmtree(log_dir)
    emit("CLEANUP_REMOVED_DIR", path=log_dir)
except Exception as e:
    emit("CLEANUP_FAILED", path=log_dir, error=e)

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Following the CLI intake and parameter orchestration established in main.py and the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) construction defined in flow.py, nodes.py provides the operational execution engine of the documentation pipeline. It defines all ten processing node classes that inherit from PocketFlow's Node and BatchNode base classes. Each node implements the canonical three-stage lifecycle—prep() for shared-state extraction and prompt preparation, exec() for LLM inference or I/O processing, and post() for mutating the centralized shared dictionary.

The module is responsible for bridging low-level filesystem ingestion with high-level cognitive synthesis. It dynamically chooses between direct single-prompt synthesis, batch map-reduce partitioning, and 1:1 deterministic file mapping based on codebase size and token constraints. To maintain high synthesis fidelity within model context boundaries, the nodes implement dynamic token budgeting algorithms, two-pass greedy file allocation, sliding-window summaries of preceding chapters, and incremental MD5 disk caching.

docs.title: DeterministicFileMapper
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class DeterministicFileMapper(Node):

A specialized Node subclass that implements a non-clustering, 1:1 file-to-chapter documentation strategy. Operating primarily in api-reference mode, it bypasses architectural clustering and instead filters candidate files through an LLM before mapping each retained file directly into an isolated chapter module. Chapters are ordered deterministically by filesystem hierarchy depth (leaf files first) to guarantee that utility dependency summaries are available before orchestrating modules are analyzed.

docs.title: prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple[str, bool, str | None, int]:

Description: Extracts the candidate file listing from shared["files"], formats each entry with its integer index and path, and generates a negative-filtering prompt via build_code_file_filter_prompt(). Returns prompt parameters and inference flags for execution.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Central blackboard state store containing "files", "project_name", and execution options.

Returns: * tuple[str, bool, str | None, int]: A 4-element tuple comprising (prompt, use_cache, thinking_level, max_tokens).

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]

        file_listing = "\n".join([f"{i} # {path}" for i, (path, _) in enumerate(files_data)])

        prompt = build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name, file_listing)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"DeterministicFileMapper prep | {len(files_data)} candidate files for filtering", dest="LOG")
        return prompt, shared.get("use_cache", True), shared.get("thinking_level", None), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000)
The method retrieves the list of (path, content) tuples from shared["files"]. It projects this list into a newline-separated manifest where each line pairs the index with the path formatted as {index} # {path}. It then delegates to build_code_file_filter_prompt() to construct the instruction set asking the LLM to discard build artifacts, package manifests, or non-code files.

docs.title: exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list[int]:

Description: Dispatches the filtering prompt to the LLM execution gateway, verifies response token boundaries, parses the returned YAML array of integer indices, and falls back to an empty list on malformed output.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): The 4-element tuple returned by prep().

Returns: * list[int]: List of integer indices corresponding to retained, valid source code files.

Raises: * Exception: Re-raises any trapped exception after logging telemetry and triggering pocketflow node retry policies.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        try:
            prompt, use_cache, thinking_level, max_tokens = prep_res
            emit("LLM_CALL_FILTER_FILES")
            log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, max_tokens)
            response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
            valid_indices = parse_yaml_response(response)
            if not isinstance(valid_indices, list):
                valid_indices = []
            return [int(idx) for idx in valid_indices]
        except Exception as e:
            emit("NODE_RETRY_ERROR", class_name=self.__class__.__name__, error=e)
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}", dest="LOG")
            raise e
The method logs diagnostic token estimation before calling call_llm(). The use_cache parameter is conditioned on self.cur_retry == 0, ensuring that any automatic retry bypasses stale cached completions. The YAML response is deserialized into native Python objects via parse_yaml_response() and normalized into a typed list[int].

docs.title: post()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: tuple, exec_res: list[int]) -> str:

Description: Constructs 1:1 module definitions for all retained file indices, computes directory-depth traversal ordering, initializes synthetic relationship structures, and registers the abstractions in shared.

Parameters: * shared (dict): The central state store to be mutated. * prep_res (tuple): The parameters emitted from prep(). * exec_res (list[int]): The list of validated integer file indices.

Returns: * str: The PocketFlow action string "default".

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        import os

        files = shared.get("files", [])
        valid_indices = set(exec_res)
        modules = []
        chapter_order = []

        for idx, (file_path, _content) in enumerate(files):
            if idx not in valid_indices:
                emit("SKIP_NON_CODE_FILE", path=file_path)
                continue

            clean_name = os.path.basename(file_path)

            modules.append(
                {"name": clean_name, "description": f"Internal API reference for `{file_path}`", "files": [idx], "original_path": file_path}
            )
            chapter_order.append(len(modules) - 1)

        shared["abstractions"] = modules
        # Sort chapter order by directory depth (deepest first, then alphabetical).
        # This ensures utility/leaf files are processed before orchestration files,
        # so their summaries are available as cross-chapter context.
        # Works universally across all languages (Python, C#, C++, Java, etc.).
        shared["chapter_order"] = sorted(
            chapter_order,
            key=lambda idx: (
                -modules[idx]["original_path"].count("/") - modules[idx]["original_path"].count(os.sep),
                modules[idx]["original_path"].lower(),
            ),
        )
        shared["relationships"] = {"summary": "Deterministic Internal API Reference.", "details": []}
        emit("DONE_DETERMINISTIC_MAPPER", count=len(modules))
        return "default"
The method builds an abstraction dictionary for every index retained by the LLM filter. Crucially, shared["chapter_order"] is sorted using a lambda key that calculates negative slash and separator counts (-path.count("/") - path.count(os.sep)). This ensures leaf modules residing deep in the directory tree (such as utilities and data models) appear first in the order. When WriteChapters runs sequentially, summaries of leaf files are synthesized and placed in the context window before high-level orchestrators are drafted.

docs.title: ContextRouter
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: class ContextRouter(Node):

A routing and context-budgeting node that inspects total codebase volume against the LLM's configured context window. It decides whether the pipeline can analyze all source code in a single prompt ("direct"), must split the files into coherent directory-level partitions ("batch"), or must follow a 1:1 file reference mapping ("deterministic").

docs.title: prep()
docs.text: This method evaluates token headroom across four sequential phases:

docs.title: 1. Prompt Overhead Calculation
docs.text:
# --- Calculate prompt overhead FIRST ---
        # 1. Prompt templates: check both IA/MA (for batching) and WC (for chapter writing)
        #    Use the largest template across all modes as worst-case estimate
        prompt_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts")
        max_template_tokens = 0
        for subdir in ["tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk"]:
            for template_name in ["map_abstractions.md", "identify_abstractions.md", "draft_chapters.md"]:
                template_path = os.path.join(prompt_dir, subdir, template_name)
                if os.path.exists(template_path):
                    with open(template_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                        t = count_tokens(f.read())
                    max_template_tokens = max(max_template_tokens, t)
The node reads prompt markdown files across all documentation modes ("tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk") to establish the worst-case template footprint (max_template_tokens). This ensures that context estimations reflect the largest possible instruction payload.

docs.title: 2. Structural Metadata Overhead
docs.text:
# 2. Directory tree (shared across IA, MA, and WC prompts)
        directory_tree = build_directory_tree(files_data)
        tree_tokens = count_tokens(directory_tree)

        # 3. Chapter listing estimate (used in WC draft_chapters prompts)
        #    Format: "N. basename (doc: path.md)" per file
        chapter_listing_estimate = "\n".join(f"{i + 1}. {os.path.basename(path)} (doc: {path}.md)" for i, (path, _) in enumerate(files_data))
        listing_tokens = count_tokens(chapter_listing_estimate)

        prompt_overhead = max_template_tokens + tree_tokens + listing_tokens
        emit(
            "CAPACITY_PROMPT_OVERHEAD",
            total=f"{prompt_overhead:,}",
            template=f"{max_template_tokens:,}",
            tree=f"{tree_tokens:,}",
            listing=f"{listing_tokens:,}",
        )
The method computes the token volume of the rendered directory tree using build_directory_tree() and constructs an estimated flat chapter listing. The sum of template tokens, tree tokens, and listing tokens constitutes the immutable prompt overhead (prompt_overhead).

docs.title: 3. Codebase Token Aggregation
docs.text:
# --- Count file content tokens ---
        total_tokens = 0
        file_token_map = []
        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
            tokens = count_tokens(entry)
            total_tokens += tokens
            file_token_map.append(tokens)

        # --- Effective limit = safety margin minus overhead ---
        safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
        effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead
        force_batch = shared.get("force_batch", False)
Each file entry is formatted with boundary headers, and its token cost is pre-computed and stored in file_token_map. The effective token limit is calculated by taking 95% of max_tokens (to maintain provider safety margins) and subtracting the calculated prompt_overhead.

docs.title: 4. Routing Decision Logic
docs.text:
if shared.get("mode", "tutorial") == "api-reference":
            emit("CAPACITY_API_REF_MODE")
            return ("deterministic", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree)

        if total_tokens > effective_limit and force_batch:
            emit(
                "CAPACITY_EXCEEDS_FORCE",
                tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}",
                limit=f"{effective_limit:,}",
                safety=f"{safety_limit:,}",
                overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}",
            )
        elif total_tokens > effective_limit:
            emit(
                "CAPACITY_EXCEEDS",
                tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}",
                limit=f"{effective_limit:,}",
                safety=f"{safety_limit:,}",
                overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}",
            )
        elif force_batch:
            emit(
                "CAPACITY_FITS_FORCE",
                tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}",
                limit=f"{effective_limit:,}",
                safety=f"{safety_limit:,}",
                overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}",
            )
        else:
            emit(
                "CAPACITY_FITS", tokens=f"{total_tokens:,}", limit=f"{effective_limit:,}", safety=f"{safety_limit:,}", overhead=f"{prompt_overhead:,}"
            )
            return ("direct", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree)

        return (
            "batch",
            files_data,
            effective_limit,
            shared.get("batch_size", 50),
            file_token_map,
            count_tokens,
            directory_tree,
        )
If mode is configured as "api-reference", the route immediately resolves to "deterministic". Otherwise, if total_tokens fits within effective_limit and force_batch is False, the route resolves to "direct". In all other circumstances (context overflow or manual batch enforcement), it routes to "batch".

docs.title: exec()
docs.text:
def exec(self, prep_res):
        route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, _count_tokens, directory_tree = prep_res
        emit_raw(
            "DEBUG",
            f"NODE EXEC | node=ContextRouter | action=route_decision | route={route} | files={len(files_data)} | effective_limit={effective_limit:,}",
            dest="LOG",
        )

        if route == "direct":
            return "direct"
        if route == "deterministic":
            return "deterministic"

        # Group by directory for coherence, with pre-computed tokens
        dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            dir_groups[os.path.dirname(path)].append((i, path, content, file_token_map[i]))

        # Build token-aware batches (never mix directories)
        batches = []
        for dirname in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
            current_batch = []
            current_tokens = 0

            for i, path, content, tokens in dir_groups[dirname]:
                # Start new batch if adding this file would exceed effective limit or file count cap
                if current_batch and (current_tokens + tokens > effective_limit or len(current_batch) >= batch_size):
                    batches.append(current_batch)
                    current_batch = []
                    current_tokens = 0

                current_batch.append((i, path, content))
                current_tokens += tokens

            # Flush remaining files in this directory
            if current_batch:
                batches.append(current_batch)

        batch_word = "batch" if len(batches) == 1 else "batches"
        emit("CAPACITY_SPLIT", count=len(batches), word=batch_word)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"NODE COMPLETE | node=ContextRouter | route={route} | batches={len(batches)}", dest="LOG")

        # Debug: show detailed batch info
        for idx, batch in enumerate(batches):
            content_tokens = sum(file_token_map[i] for i, p, _c in batch)
            emit("CAPACITY_BATCH_DEBUG", index=idx, file_count=len(batch), tokens=f"{content_tokens:,}", limit=f"{effective_limit:,}")
            for i, p, _c in batch:
                emit("BATCH_FILE_ITEM", index=i, path=p)

        # Store directory tree for later use
        self._directory_tree = directory_tree

        return batches
When handling a "batch" decision, exec() groups candidate files by directory name (dir_groups). It aggregates files into discrete batches without mixing directories across batch boundaries. A new batch is initialized whenever adding a file would cause total batch tokens to exceed effective_limit or exceed the configured batch_size. The resulting partitions are stored as a list of batches.

docs.title: post()
docs.text:
def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"ContextRouter post | route={'batch' if isinstance(exec_res, list) else exec_res}", dest="LOG")
        if exec_res == "direct":
            return "direct"
        if exec_res == "deterministic":
            return "deterministic"
        shared["file_batches"] = exec_res
        # Reuse directory tree built during prep()
        shared["directory_tree"] = getattr(self, "_directory_tree", build_directory_tree(shared["files"]))
        return "batch"
The method inspects the execution result. If "direct" or "deterministic", it emits that action token directly to drive conditional PocketFlow branch transitions. If batches were compiled, it saves them to shared["file_batches"], preserves the rendered directory_tree, and returns the "batch" action string.

docs.text:
def exec(self, item):
        batch_index = item["batch_index"]
        files = item["files"]
        emit("LLM_CALL_MAP_ABSTRACTIONS", batch_index=batch_index, file_count=len(files))

        context = ""
        for i, path, content in files:
            context += f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"

        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("map_abstractions", mode=item.get("mode", "tutorial"))

        language = item.get("language", "english")
        language_instruction = f"Output language MUST be entirely in {language.capitalize()}. " if language.lower() != "english" else ""
        name_lang_hint = f" (in {language.capitalize()})" if language.lower() != "english" else ""
        desc_lang_hint = f" (in {language.capitalize()})" if language.lower() != "english" else ""

        prompt = prompt_template.format(
            project_name=item["project_name"],
            context=context,
            language_instruction=language_instruction,
            name_lang_hint=name_lang_hint,
            desc_lang_hint=desc_lang_hint,
            directory_tree=item.get("directory_tree", "Not available"),
        )

        token_usage = {
            "file_content": count_tokens(context),
            "directory_tree": count_tokens(item.get("directory_tree", "")),
        }
        token_usage["overhead"] = count_tokens(prompt) - sum(token_usage.values())
        log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, item["max_tokens"], token_usage=token_usage)
        for i, path, _content in files:
            emit("BATCH_FILE_ITEM", index=i, path=path)
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"])

        abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)

        validated_abstractions = []
        if isinstance(abstractions, list):
            for obj in abstractions:
                if isinstance(obj, dict) and "name" in obj and "description" in obj and "file_indices" in obj:
                    import re

                    validated_indices = []
                    for idx_entry in obj["file_indices"]:
                        nums = re.findall(r"\d+", str(idx_entry))
                        if nums:
                            validated_indices.append(int(nums[0]))
                    if validated_indices:
                        validated_abstractions.append(
                            {"name": obj["name"], "description": obj["description"], "files": sorted(set(validated_indices))}
                        )
        return validated_abstractions
For each batch, the method constructs a formatted file context string, loads the mode-specific map_abstractions.md template via load_prompt_template(), and invokes the LLM. It parses the resulting YAML completion, extracts digits from the file_indices array via regular expressions, and constructs validated abstraction dictionaries containing "name", "description", and "files".

def prep(self, shared):
        repo_url = shared.get("repo_url")
        local_dir = shared.get("local_dir")
        project_name = shared.get("project_name")

        if not project_name:
            # Basic name derivation from URL or directory

        )

        exclude_patterns = shared["exclude_patterns"]
        max_file_size = shared["max_file_size"]

        return {
            "repo_url": repo_url,
            "local_dir": local_dir,
            "token": shared.get("github_token"),

docs.text:
def exec(self, prep_res):
        source = prep_res["repo_url"] or prep_res["local_dir"]
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"NODE EXEC | node=FetchRepo | action=crawl_files | source={source}", dest="LOG")

        if prep_res["repo_url"]:
            emit("CRAWL_REPOSITORY", url=prep_res["repo_url"])
            result = crawl_github_files(
                repo_url=prep_res["repo_url"],
                token=prep_res["token"],
                include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
                exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
                max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
                use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
            )
        else:
            emit("CRAWL_DIRECTORY", path=prep_res["local_dir"])

            result = crawl_local_files(
                directory=prep_res["local_dir"],
                include_patterns=prep_res["include_patterns"],
                exclude_patterns=prep_res["exclude_patterns"],
                max_file_size=prep_res["max_file_size"],
                use_relative_paths=prep_res["use_relative_paths"],
            )

        # Convert dict to list of tuples: [(path, content), ...]
        files_list = list(result.get("files", {}).items())
        if len(files_list) == 0:
            raise ValueError("No matching files found. Check your directory and include/exclude patterns.")

        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"NODE COMPLETE | node=FetchRepo | files_found={len(files_list)}", dest="LOG")
        return files_list
Routes ingestion to crawl_github_files() when repo_url is populated, or crawl_local_files() when local_dir is defined. It transforms the returned dictionary mapping of {path: content} into an ordered list of (path, content) tuples and validates that at least one file was captured.

Visibility: Public Signature: class IdentifyAbstractions(Node):

The single-prompt discovery node used when the entire codebase fits comfortably within the LLM's effective context window ("direct" route). It inspects the complete file corpus alongside the directory hierarchy to identify overarching concepts, systems, and architectural patterns.

def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]  # Get project name
        language = shared.get("language", "english")  # Get language
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)  # Get use_cache flag, default to True
        max_abstraction_num = shared.get("max_abstraction_num", 10)  # Get max_abstraction_num, default to 10
        thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level", None)

        # Helper to create context from files, respecting limits (basic example)
        def create_llm_context(files_data):
            # Retrieve max tokens limit
            max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)

            safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)

            context = ""
            current_tokens = 0

            for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
                entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"

                entry_tokens = count_tokens(entry)

                if current_tokens + entry_tokens > safety_limit:
                    emit("WARN_CONTEXT_TRUNCATED", index=i, path=path, limit=safety_limit)
                    break

                context += entry
                current_tokens += entry_tokens

            return context

        context = create_llm_context(files_data)
        directory_tree = build_directory_tree(files_data)
        current_tokens = count_tokens(context)
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"IdentifyAbstractions prep | context_tokens={current_tokens:,} | files={len(files_data)}", dest="LOG")
        return (
            context,
            directory_tree,
            len(files_data),
            project_name,
            language,
            use_cache,
            max_abstraction_num,
            thinking_level,
            shared.get("advanced_mode", False),
            shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
            shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
        )  # Return all parameters (11-element tuple)

                if not isinstance(item["file_indices"], list):
                    raise ValueError(f"file_indices is not a list in item: {item}")

                # Validate indices
                import re

                validated_indices = []
                for idx_entry in item["file_indices"]:
                    try:
                        idx_str = str(idx_entry).split("#")[0].strip()
                        # Split by '-' to handle ranges
                        if "-" in idx_str:
                            parts = idx_str.split("-")
                            if len(parts) == 2:
                                start_idx = int(re.findall(r"\d+", parts[0])[0])
                                end_idx = int(re.findall(r"\d+", parts[1])[0])
                                validated_indices.extend(idx for idx in range(start_idx, end_idx + 1) if 0 <= idx < total_files_count)
                                continue
                        # Find integers in the string
                        nums = re.findall(r"\d+", idx_str)
                        if nums:
                            idx = int(nums[0])
                            if 0 <= idx < total_files_count:
                                validated_indices.append(idx)
                    except (ValueError, TypeError, IndexError):
                        emit("WARN_PARSE_INDEX", entry=idx_entry, name=item["name"])
                        continue

                item["files"] = sorted(set(validated_indices))
                # Store only the required fields
                validated_abstractions.append(
                    {
                        "name": item["name"],  # Potentially translated name
                        "description": item["description"],  # Potentially translated description
                        "files": item["files"],
                    }
                )

            emit("DONE_IDENTIFIED_ABSTRACTIONS", count=len(validated_abstractions))
            return validated_abstractions
Validates the structural integrity of the returned YAML payload. It parses single integers, string annotations (e.g., "3 # utils/parser.py"), and index ranges (e.g., "5-8"), ensuring all resolved indices fall strictly within the bounds [0, total_files_count).

Visibility: Public Signature: class AnalyzeRelationships(Node):

A topological analysis node that models inter-abstraction dependencies. It evaluates how the discovered abstractions interact and produce architectural dataflows. To prevent context window exhaustion when presenting code snippets across multiple abstractions, it executes a budget-aware, two-pass file snippet allocation algorithm.

docs.title: prep()
docs.text: This method prepares relationship context across three sequential phases:

docs.title: 1. Abstraction Metadata Context
docs.text:
# Create context with abstraction names, indices, descriptions, and relevant file snippets

        all_relevant_indices = set()
        abstraction_info_for_prompt = []
        for i, abstr in enumerate(abstractions):
            # Use 'files' which contains indices directly

            # Abstraction name and description might be translated already

            context += info_line + "\n"

            all_relevant_indices.update(abstr["files"])
Builds an enumerated textual summary of all abstractions, pairing their integer indices with descriptions and associated file indices.

docs.title: 2. Two-Pass Dynamic Budget Allocation
docs.text:
# Pre-compute file token sizes for all abstractions
        abstr_file_data = []  # list of [(idx, path, content, tokens), ...] per abstraction
        for abstr in abstractions:
            sized = []
            for idx in abstr["files"]:
                if 0 <= idx < len(files_data):
                    path, file_content = files_data[idx]
                    entry = f"\n--- File: {idx} # {path} ---\n{file_content}\n"
                    sized.append((idx, path, file_content, count_tokens(entry)))
            # Sort largest first (most architecturally significant)
            sized.sort(key=lambda x: x[3], reverse=True)
            abstr_file_data.append(sized)

        # Two-pass allocation:
        # Pass 1: give each abstraction an equal share, track unused
        # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions that need more
        per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
        included_indices = set()
        # Track what each abstraction selected and what's left over
        abstr_results = []  # list of (included_files, remaining_files, unused_budget)

        for _i, sized in enumerate(abstr_file_data):
            budget = per_abstr_budget
            included_files = []
            remaining_files = []
            for idx, path, file_content, tokens in sized:
                if idx in included_indices:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                    continue
                if tokens <= budget:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                    budget -= tokens
                    included_indices.add(idx)
                else:
                    remaining_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
            abstr_results.append((included_files, remaining_files, budget))

        # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions with remaining files
        total_unused = sum(r[2] for r in abstr_results)
        if total_unused > 0:
            for i, (included_files, remaining_files, _unused) in enumerate(abstr_results):
                if not remaining_files or total_unused <= 0:
                    continue
                still_remaining = []
                for idx, path, file_content, tokens in remaining_files:
                    if idx in included_indices:
                        included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                        continue
                    if tokens <= total_unused:
                        included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                        total_unused -= tokens
                        included_indices.add(idx)
                    else:
                        still_remaining.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                abstr_results[i] = (included_files, still_remaining, 0)
Computes the token weight of every relevant file and sorts them by size descending. In Pass 1, it partitions total_budget equally across all abstractions. If an abstraction exhausts its files before spending its allocation, the leftover tokens are pooled into total_unused. In Pass 2, total_unused is dynamically redistributed to abstractions that have remaining unrepresented files. Files already included in prior abstractions are deduplicated and tagged with a pointer reference.
