This initialization phase ensures that the target filesystem path docs/api exists prior to disk operations. It maps the internal execution mode string to localized UI strings via get(), dynamically configuring the primary site title used in page headers and browser tab labels.

docs.title: Phase 2: LLM-Assisted Nav Grouping & Hierarchy Resolution
docs.text:
When operating in api-reference mode with more than five chapters, the function invokes an LLM to cluster flat module listings into functional architectural sections:

    sections = None
    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"NAV GROUPING CHECK | mode={mode} | module_count={len(chapter_files)} | threshold=6", dest="LOG")
    if mode == "api-reference" and len(chapter_files) > 5:
        try:
            chapter_summaries = prep_res.get("chapter_summaries", [])
            module_entries = []
            for i, cf in enumerate(chapter_files):
                summary = chapter_summaries[i] if i < len(chapter_summaries) and chapter_summaries[i] else cf["description"]
                module_entries.append(f"- {cf['module_name']}: {summary}")
            module_list = "\n".join(module_entries)

            # Load grouping prompt template
            prompt_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "prompts", "common", "group_modules.md")
            with open(prompt_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                group_template = f.read()

            language = prep_res.get("language", "english")
            language_note = f"Section names MUST be in {language}." if language.lower() != "english" else ""

            group_prompt = group_template.format(
                project_name=project_name,
                module_count=len(chapter_files),
                module_list=module_list,
                directory_tree=prep_res.get("directory_tree", "N/A"),
                language_note=language_note,
            )

            emit("LLM_CALL_GROUPING", count=len(chapter_files))

            log_token_estimation("NavGrouping", group_prompt, prep_res.get("max_tokens", 100000))
            group_response = call_llm(group_prompt, use_cache=prep_res.get("use_cache", True), thinking_level=prep_res.get("thinking_level"))
            parsed = parse_yaml_response(group_response)
            sections = parsed.get("sections", parsed) if isinstance(parsed, dict) else None

            if sections:
                # Validate: ensure all modules are covered
                grouped_modules = collect_all_modules(sections)
                ungrouped = [cf["module_name"] for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] not in grouped_modules]
                if ungrouped:
                    sections.append({"name": get("UI_OTHER"), "modules": ungrouped})

                nav_lines = build_grouped_nav(sections, chapter_files, indent=4)
                nav_lines.insert(0, "    - api/index.md")
                nav_label = mode_labels.get(mode, "Documentation")
                nav_snippet = f"nav:\n  - {nav_label}:\n" + "\n".join(nav_lines)
                emit("DONE_GROUPING", count=len(sections))
            else:
                emit("GROUP_EMPTY_FALLBACK")
                nav_snippet = prep_res["nav_snippet"]

        except Exception as e:
            emit("GROUP_ERROR_FALLBACK", error=e)
            emit_raw("ERROR", f"LLM grouping failed: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}", dest="LOG")
            nav_snippet = prep_res["nav_snippet"]
            sections = None
    else:
        nav_snippet = prep_res["nav_snippet"]

This phase compiles chapter summaries, module paths, and directory layout strings into an LLM prompt using group_modules.md. The prompt is dispatched through call_llm() with token tracking handled by token_utils.py. The resulting YAML is parsed with parse_yaml_response. If the LLM omits modules, the method groups the missing files under an Other section via get("UI_OTHER"). If the LLM call fails or raises an exception, the pipeline falls back gracefully to prep_res["nav_snippet"].

docs.title: Phase 3: Site Configuration and Client Script Generation
docs.text:
Generates and writes the site configuration (mkdocs.yml) and JavaScript assets:

    # --- Generate mkdocs.yml ---
    lang_code_map = {
        "vietnamese": "vi",
        "chinese": "zh",
        "japanese": "ja",
        "korean": "ko",
        "french": "fr",
        "spanish": "es",
        "german": "de",
        "portuguese": "pt",
        "russian": "ru",
        "thai": "th",
        "indonesian": "id",
        "arabic": "ar",
    }
    language = prep_res.get("language", "english")
    lang_code = lang_code_map.get(language.lower(), "")
    mkdocs_config = build_mkdocs_config(site_title, nav_snippet, include_home=True, lang_code=lang_code)
    mkdocs_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, "mkdocs.yml")
    with open(mkdocs_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(mkdocs_config)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=mkdocs_filepath)

    # --- Generate javascripts/mermaid-init.js ---
    js_dir = os.path.join(output_path, "docs", "javascripts")
    os.makedirs(js_dir, exist_ok=True)
    js_filepath = os.path.join(js_dir, "mermaid-init.js")
    with open(js_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(build_mermaid_init_js())
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=js_filepath)

The system maps the user's language name to an ISO 639-1 code, configuring MkDocs Material localization settings such as search indexes and UI labels. It then generates mkdocs.yml using build_mkdocs_config() and writes mermaid-init.js to ensure interactive diagrams render correctly in the browser.

docs.title: Phase 4: Landing Pages & Navigation Manifest Generation
docs.text:
Constructs the top-level HTML redirect and the main API index landing page:

    # --- Generate docs/index.md — homepage redirect to api/ ---
    mode_label = mode_labels.get(mode, "Documentation")
    home_index_path = os.path.join(output_path, "docs", "index.md")
    home_content = f'# {project_name}\n\n<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; url=api/">\n\n[→ {mode_label}](api/index.md)\n'
    with open(home_index_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(home_content)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=home_index_path)

    # --- Generate docs/api/index.md — section landing page ---
    if sections:
        chapter_index_label = get("UI_CHAPTER_INDEX")
        chapters_label = get("UI_CHAPTERS")
        index_lines = [
            f"# {project_name} — {mode_label}",
            "",
            f"{mode_label} — **{project_name}** — **{len(chapter_files)}** {chapters_label}.",
            "",
            f"## {chapter_index_label}",
            "",
        ]
        build_index_sections(index_lines, sections, chapter_files)
        index_content = "\n".join(index_lines)
    else:
        # Build a rich flat index with module listing table
        chapter_summaries = prep_res.get("chapter_summaries", [])
        chapter_index_label = get("UI_CHAPTER_INDEX")
        chapters_label = get("UI_CHAPTERS")
        th_chapter = get("UI_TH_CHAPTER")
        th_description = get("UI_TH_DESCRIPTION")
        index_lines = [
            f"# {project_name} — {mode_label}",
            "",
            f"{mode_label} — **{project_name}** — **{len(chapter_files)}** {chapters_label}.",
            "",
            f"## {chapter_index_label}",
            "",
            f"| {th_chapter} | {th_description} |",
            "|---------|-------------|",
        ]
        for i, cf in enumerate(chapter_files):
            dir_path = os.path.dirname(cf.get("original_path", "")) or ""
            display = f"{dir_path}/{cf['module_name']}" if dir_path else cf["module_name"]
            summary = chapter_summaries[i] if i < len(chapter_summaries) and chapter_summaries[i] else cf["description"]
            # Truncate and sanitize for table cell (replace pipes and newlines)
            summary = summary.replace("|", "—").replace("\n", " ").strip()
            if len(summary) > 200:
                summary = summary[:197] + "..."
            index_lines.append(f"| [{display}]({cf['filename']}) | {summary} |")
        index_lines.append("")
        index_content = "\n".join(index_lines)
    api_index_filepath = os.path.join(api_docs_path, "index.md")
    with open(api_index_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(index_content)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=api_index_filepath)

    # --- Write nav_snippet.yml ---
    nav_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, "docs", "nav_snippet.yml")
    with open(nav_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(nav_snippet)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=nav_filepath)

The site creates a root landing page at docs/index.md with an HTTP <meta> refresh tag pointing to api/. For the main section page at docs/api/index.md, it renders either hierarchical markdown tables via build_index_sections() (when sections are defined) or a flat Markdown table. In the flat fallback, summary descriptions are cleaned by stripping line breaks, replacing Markdown pipe characters with em dashes (—), and truncating strings to 200 characters to prevent broken table formatting.

docs.title: Phase 5: Deterministic Link Normalization and Serialization
docs.text:
Repairs cross-chapter links across the documentation and writes out the final chapter files:

    # --- Normalize cross-chapter links ---
    normalize_chapter_links(chapter_files)

    # --- Write chapter files ---
    for chapter_info in chapter_files:
        chapter_filepath = os.path.join(api_docs_path, chapter_info["filename"])
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(chapter_filepath), exist_ok=True)
        with open(chapter_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(chapter_info["content"])
        emit("FILE_WROTE", path=chapter_filepath)

This final phase runs normalize_chapter_links() to adjust markdown links between chapters based on their final directory locations. The modified chapters are then written out to disk under docs/api/, creating any nested subdirectories on demand.

docs.title: write_standalone_output()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def write_standalone_output(output_path, prep_res, chapter_files, ui):

Description: Serializes documentation when --mkdocs output is disabled. Writes independent Markdown chapters, generates a root index.md, and compiles a combined full_content.md document containing anchor-based navigation links.

Parameters: * output_path (str): Destination directory path where standalone Markdown files are saved. * prep_res (dict): Metadata dictionary providing index_content. * chapter_files (list[dict]): Collection of chapter dictionaries containing filename and content. * ui (dict): Localized UI dictionary providing terms such as toc and chapter.

Returns: * None

Raises: * OSError / IOError: Raised if directory creation or file operations fail.

docs.title: Phase 1: Index and Chapter Writing
docs.text:
Writes the main landing page and serializes each chapter file:

    index_content = prep_res["index_content"]
    emit("COMBINE_FORMAT_STANDALONE")
    emit("COMBINE_CHAPTER_COUNT", count=len(chapter_files))

    # Write index.md
    index_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, "index.md")
    with open(index_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(index_content)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=index_filepath)

    # Write chapter files
    for chapter_info in chapter_files:
        chapter_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, chapter_info["filename"])
        with open(chapter_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(chapter_info["content"])
        emit("FILE_WROTE", path=chapter_filepath)

This initial phase writes index.md directly into the target root directory using the pre-rendered index_content payload from prep_res. Each chapter dictionary is then written to its relative file path, ensuring all individual chapter files are persisted to disk.

docs.title: Phase 2: Combined Document Assembly (full_content.md)
docs.text:
Merges all chapters into a single concatenated file with anchor tags and a Table of Contents:

    # Create full_content.md
    toc_lines = [f"# {ui['toc']}\n"]
    full_content_lines = []

    for i, chapter_info in enumerate(chapter_files):
        content = chapter_info["content"]
        title_line = content.split("\n", 1)[0]
        if title_line.startswith("# "):
            title = title_line[2:].strip()
        else:
            title = f"{ui['chapter']} {i + 1}"

        toc_lines.append(f"- [{title}](#chapter-{i + 1})")
        full_content_lines.append(f'<a id="chapter-{i + 1}"></a>\n')
        full_content_lines.append(content)
        full_content_lines.append("\n---\n")

    full_content = "\n".join(toc_lines) + "\n\n" + "\n".join(full_content_lines)
    full_content_filepath = os.path.join(output_path, "full_content.md")
    with open(full_content_filepath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(full_content)
    emit("FILE_WROTE", path=full_content_filepath)

The function generates a Table of Contents by extracting top-level # headings from each chapter's content or falling back to a default Chapter {N} label. Each chapter is wrapped with an explicit HTML anchor (<a id="chapter-N"></a>) and separated by horizontal rules (---), assembling the entire documentation set into a single portable file (full_content.md).

docs.title: build_index_sections()
docs.text:
Visibility: Internal Signature: def build_index_sections(lines, sections, chapter_files, level=3):

Description: Recursively constructs Markdown index tables for grouped sections. For each section, it outputs a Markdown header scaled by level, writes a table mapping chapters to their descriptions, and descends into any nested children sections.

Parameters: * lines (list[str]): Accumulator list of Markdown strings appended in place. * sections (list[dict]): Hierarchical list of section definitions. * chapter_files (list[dict]): Available chapter metadata items. * level (int, optional): Markdown heading depth (###, ####, etc.). Defaults to 3.

Returns: * None (mutates lines in-place).

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def build_index_sections(lines, sections, chapter_files, level=3):
    heading = "#" * level
    for section in sections:
        lines.append(f"{heading} {section['name']}")
        lines.append("")
        if section.get("modules"):
            lines.append(f"| {get('UI_TH_CHAPTER')} | {get('UI_TH_DESCRIPTION')} |")
            lines.append("|---------|-------------|")
            for mod_name in section["modules"]:
                match = next((cf for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] == mod_name), None)
                if match:
                    display = mod_name
                    # Use description, but if it's the generic mapper description, extract from content
                    desc = match["description"]
                    if desc.startswith("Internal API reference"):
                        content_lines = match["content"].strip().split("\n")
                        for cl in content_lines:
                            cs = cl.strip()
                            if cs and not cs.startswith(("---", "#", "```", "title:", "sidebar_position:")):
                                desc = cs[:120]
                                break
                    lines.append(f"| [{display}]({match['filename']}) | {desc} |")
            lines.append("")
        for child in section.get("children", []):
            build_index_sections(lines, [child], chapter_files, level + 1)

This helper handles fallback description extraction. If a module's description field contains a generic string such as "Internal API reference", it parses the raw Markdown content to find the first meaningful text line that is not a heading, frontmatter block, or code fence, truncating it to 120 characters for clean table formatting.

docs.title: normalize_chapter_links()
docs.text:
Visibility: Internal Signature: def normalize_chapter_links(chapter_files):

Description: Normalizes cross-chapter Markdown links across all generated files. Resolves relative link paths between chapters in different directories based on their target filenames.

Parameters: * chapter_files (list[dict]): Chapter file dictionaries containing filename and content. Mutated in-place.

Returns: * None (mutates chapter_files items in-place).

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

docs.title: Phase 1: Canonical Path Lookup & Ambiguity Resolution
docs.text:
Builds a filename lookup table and identifies potential collisions across directories:

    # Build lookup: various path forms → canonical filename
    filename_lookup = {}
    ambiguous_basenames = set()
    for cf in chapter_files:
        fname = cf["filename"]  # e.g. "CoreService/AccountingService.cs.md"
        filename_lookup[fname] = fname
        basename = fname.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        if basename in filename_lookup and filename_lookup[basename] != fname:
            ambiguous_basenames.add(basename)
        else:
            filename_lookup[basename] = fname

    # Remove ambiguous basenames (same name in different dirs)
    for ab in ambiguous_basenames:
        filename_lookup.pop(ab, None)

The method registers both full relative paths (CoreService/AccountingService.cs.md) and simple base names (AccountingService.cs.md) in a lookup table. If identical file names appear across multiple directories, those entries are flagged as ambiguous and removed from the base lookup, preventing incorrect link rewriting.

docs.title: Phase 2: In-place Link Substitution & Relative Directory Re-computation
docs.text:
Parses Markdown links with regular expressions, calculates corrected relative paths using os.path.relpath, and preserves URI anchors:

    link_pattern = re.compile(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)#]+\.md)(#[^)]*)?\)")
    fixed_count = 0

    for cf in chapter_files:
        current_dir = os.path.dirname(cf["filename"])  # e.g. "CoreService"

        def fix_link(match, _dir=current_dir):
            nonlocal fixed_count
            text, target, anchor = match.group(1), match.group(2), match.group(3) or ""
            if target.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
                return match.group(0)
            # Try resolving the target as-is (LLM copied verbatim from index)
            canonical = filename_lookup.get(target)
            if not canonical:
                # Try resolving relative to current dir
                resolved = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(_dir, target)).replace("\\", "/")
                canonical = filename_lookup.get(resolved)
            if canonical:
                correct_rel = os.path.relpath(canonical, _dir).replace("\\", "/") if _dir else canonical
                if correct_rel != target:
                    fixed_count += 1
                return f"[{text}]({correct_rel}{anchor})"
            return match.group(0)  # Unknown target — leave as-is

        cf["content"] = link_pattern.sub(fix_link, cf["content"])

    if fixed_count:
        emit_raw("DEBUG", f"LINK NORMALIZATION | fixed {fixed_count} cross-chapter links", dest="LOG")

The inner replacement closure fix_link matches Markdown links ending in .md and ignores external HTTP/HTTPS URLs. It resolves targets against the lookup table, normalizes paths across Windows and POSIX systems with .replace("\\", "/"), and calculates the relative path from the current chapter's directory using os.path.relpath(). Any original URI hash anchors (#anchor) are preserved.

docs.title: MERMAID_INIT_JS
docs.text:
Visibility: Internal Constant Signature: MERMAID_INIT_JS: str

Description: JavaScript snippet embedded into generated MkDocs sites (docs/javascripts/mermaid-init.js) to handle Mermaid diagram rendering and client-side initialization.

// Mermaid initialization for MkDocs Material.
//
// Material for MkDocs targets .mermaid class for its own color overrides.
// By using .mermaid-raw, diagrams render with Mermaid's default theme:
// yellow subgraph backgrounds, lavender nodes, clean rectangles.
//
// pymdownx.superfences fence_code_format wraps content as:
//   <pre class="mermaid-raw"><code>flowchart TD ...</code></pre>
// Mermaid expects the diagram text directly in the target element,
// so we unwrap the <code> child before calling mermaid.run().
(function() {
  function initMermaid() {
    if (typeof mermaid === 'undefined') return;
    try {
      // Unwrap: move <code> text content up to <pre> and remove <code>
      document.querySelectorAll('pre.mermaid-raw > code').forEach(function(code) {
        var pre = code.parentElement;
        pre.textContent = code.textContent;
      });
      mermaid.initialize({
        startOnLoad: false,
        theme: 'default',
        securityLevel: 'loose'
      });
      mermaid.run({ querySelector: '.mermaid-raw' }).catch(function(err) {
        console.warn('Mermaid render error:', err);
      });
    } catch (e) {
      console.warn('Mermaid init error:', e);
    }
  }
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', initMermaid);
  } else {
    initMermaid();
  }
})();

This client-side script initializes once the DOM is ready (DOMContentLoaded). It pulls code content out of nested <code> tags, configures Mermaid with startOnLoad: false, theme: 'default', and securityLevel: 'loose', and renders diagrams matching .mermaid-raw. Any rendering or initialization errors are caught and logged to the browser console without breaking page execution.

docs.title: Pipeline Preparation Context (prep_res)
docs.text:
The dictionary passed into write_mkdocs_output and write_standalone_output, containing configuration flags, cached artifacts, and localization settings.

Field Type Description project_name str Display name of the inspected codebase or repository. mode str Documentation mode: "tutorial", "advanced", "sdk", or "api-reference". chapter_summaries list[str] Optional module descriptions used when rendering tables of contents. language str Target language for documentation (e.g., "english", "vietnamese", "japanese"). directory_tree str Text representation of the repository's file structure. max_tokens int Token budget ceiling used for token estimation logging. use_cache bool Flag indicating whether LLM caching is active. thinking_level str / int / None Reasoning budget or thinking configuration for LLM generation. nav_snippet str Default precomputed navigation YAML snippet. index_content str Pre-rendered markdown index content (used primarily by write_standalone_output).

docs.title: Chapter File Metadata Object (chapter_info / cf)
docs.text:
Represents an individual generated documentation chapter, stored within chapter_files: list[dict].

Field Type Description filename str Target relative file path (e.g., "services/order_service.py.md"). module_name str Identifier matching the source module (e.g., "order_service.py"). description str Short synopsis of the chapter or module responsibilities. original_path str Original file path within the source repository. content str Markdown text content of the chapter (mutated by link normalization).

docs.title: Navigation Section Node (sections)
docs.text:
Hierarchical data structure parsed from LLM YAML output or constructed manually to define the MkDocs navigation tree.

Field Type Description name str Section title displayed in the MkDocs navigation sidebar. modules list[str] Optional list of module names assigned to this section. children list[dict] Optional list of nested section nodes, enabling multi-level navigation.

docs.title: UI Localization Map (ui)
docs.text:
Localization dictionary passed to write_standalone_output to provide localized headers and labels.

Field Type Description toc str Localized label for the Table of Contents header (e.g., "Table of Contents" or "Mục lục"). chapter str Localized label for generic chapter references (e.g., "Chapter" or "Chương").

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module implements defensive strategies to handle LLM parsing failures, malformed input trees, and cross-chapter link resolution:

  1. LLM Section Grouping Fallback: In write_mkdocs_output, the LLM grouping call is wrapped in a broad try...except Exception block. If network calls fail, token budgets are exceeded, or the model outputs malformed YAML, the exception is caught, logged with traceback.format_exc(), and the pipeline falls back to prep_res["nav_snippet"].

  2. Orphaned Module Recovery: When LLM-generated section groupings omit input files, write_mkdocs_output uses collect_all_modules() to identify missing entries. Any orphaned modules are appended to a fallback section titled get("UI_OTHER"), ensuring all generated documentation chapters remain reachable in site navigation.

  3. Ambiguous Filename Collision Handling: In normalize_chapter_links, repositories containing identically named files across different directories (e.g., pkg_a/index.py.md and pkg_b/index.py.md) are tracked in ambiguous_basenames. Colliding entries are excluded from base name lookups, preventing the normalizer from rewriting links to incorrect relative destinations.

  4. Client-Side Mermaid Fail-Safe: The embedded JavaScript in MERMAID_INIT_JS wraps diagram unwrapping and rendering logic in nested try...catch blocks and handles asynchronous errors via .catch(). This isolates diagram rendering failures and prevents unhandled exceptions from breaking other page functionality.

docs.title: output.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/output.py

Following the persistent documentation generation and rendering workflows established in utils/mkdocs.py, utils/output.py provides the foundational operational observability, localized terminal presentation, and structured file logging subsystem for the entire codebase.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/output.py module serves as the centralized communications bridge and presentation gateway across all stages of the documentation pipeline. It decouples core pipeline logic from standard I/O streams, terminal escape styling, and language localization concerns. By formalizing every user-facing message into an external declarative string registry (utils/strings.csv), the module eliminates hardcoded console text and ensures complete internationalization (i18n) across heterogeneous runtime environments.

Architecturally, the subsystem establishes a dual-destination dispatch pattern that coordinates between ANSI-colored terminal streams (sys.stdout) and persistent, timestamped file-based loggers (logging.FileHandler). To support localized operation without human translation overhead, the module embeds an automated runtime self-localization loop: when configured with a non-English language, it detects untranslated or missing keys in the CSV registry, compiles an ad-hoc translation prompt, queries an external Large Language Model via utils/call_llm.py, and persists the resulting translations back into disk storage with UTF-8 BOM encoding.

The diagram below illustrates the complete operational lifecycle of utils/output.py, tracing system initialization, dynamic internationalization loading, prompt-based LLM self-translation, and runtime message dispatch across styled terminal output and disk loggers.

docs.title: init()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None, debug=False) -> None:

Description: Initializes the global state of the output subsystem. It resolves the absolute file path of utils/strings.csv, normalizes the user's requested language identifier for column lookups and display names, configures caching and debug flags, loads all static string mappings into memory, and executes automated runtime translation checks for non-English executions. This function must be executed in main.py prior to calling any message emission functions.

Parameters: * language (str): Target language name (e.g., "english", "Vietnamese"). Case-insensitive; internally normalized to lowercase for column retrieval and capitalized for terminal logs. Defaults to "english". * use_cache (bool): Directs whether automated translation LLM requests should consult and populate the persistent cache managed by utils/call_llm.py. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None): Reasoning effort level passed down to the model provider during translation requests. Defaults to None. * debug (bool): Global debug toggle controlling the suppression or pass-through of debug-gated messages (DBOTH, DSTDOUT, DEBUG). Defaults to False.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised directly. File resolution or network exceptions occurring during automated translation are caught, reported, and handled with safe fallback mechanics.

Example: 

# Initializing output system with custom language and debug logging
init(language="vietnamese", use_cache=True, thinking_level="low", debug=True)

The core implementation configures module globals and orchestrates string loading followed by translation:

def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None, debug=False):
    """Initialize the output system: load strings.csv, set language, auto-translate missing.

    Must be called from main() after parsing CLI arguments but before any emit() calls.

    Args:
        language: Target language name (e.g., "Vietnamese").
        use_cache: Whether LLM caching is enabled (passed to translation calls).
        thinking_level: LLM thinking level (passed to translation calls).
    """
    global _language, _lang_col, _csv_path, _use_cache, _thinking_level, _debug
    _language = language.capitalize()
    _lang_col = language.lower()
    _csv_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "strings.csv")
    _use_cache = use_cache
    _thinking_level = thinking_level
    _debug = debug
    _load_strings()
    _auto_translate()

The initialization procedure establishes process-wide singletons within the module namespace. By calculating _csv_path using os.path.abspath(__file__), the system avoids relative path resolution errors when the root execution directory varies across invocations. The dual assignment of _language (via .capitalize()) and _lang_col (via .lower()) ensures that human-readable console banners display proper nouns (e.g., "Vietnamese") while maintaining case-insensitive column queries against the underlying CSV header row.

docs.title: emit()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def emit(key: str, suffix: str = "", **kwargs: object) -> None:

Description: Dispatches a localized, styled message to terminal standard output and/or the active file logger based on a symbolic key registered in strings.csv. It retrieves the string template, safely interpolates dynamic keyword arguments via _format_safe(), appends an optional unformatted suffix (e.g., token counters), applies destination and debug filtering rules, wraps the terminal message in ANSI escape codes, and executes logging.

Parameters: * key (str): The unique identifier matching a STRING_KEY record in strings.csv (e.g., "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER"). * suffix (str): Optional plain text appended directly to the formatted text without undergoing template variable substitution. Defaults to "". * **kwargs (object): Arbitrary named parameters matching the {placeholder} tokens declared within the registered message template.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised. If an unregistered key is supplied, the method defensively prints a formatted notice [UNKNOWN STRING: {key}] to standard output to prevent application termination while avoiding silent information loss.

Example: 

# Emitting a chapter write event with dynamic parameters and token suffix
emit("LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER", chapter_num=1, name="flow")

The implementation routes messages according to destinations, debug flags, and color maps:

def emit(key, suffix="", **kwargs):
    """Emit a translatable string to stdout and/or log file.

    Args:
        key: String key from strings.csv (e.g., "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER").
        suffix: Optional extra text appended after the main message (e.g., token breakdown).
        **kwargs: Variables to substitute into the string template.
    """
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        # Fallback for unknown keys — print raw so nothing is silently lost
        print(f"[UNKNOWN STRING: {key}]")
        return

    text = _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)
    if suffix:
        text = text + suffix

    level = entry["level"]
    dest = entry["dest"]

    # D-prefixed destinations (DBOTH, DSTDOUT): debug-gated console output.
    # Without --debug, suppress console but always log. Preserves original color from LEVEL.
    if dest.startswith("D"):
        if _debug:
            dest = dest[1:]  # DBOTH → BOTH, DSTDOUT → STDOUT
        else:
            dest = "LOG"

    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _logger.log(LOG_LEVELS.get(level, logging.INFO), text)

The function incorporates specialized routing logic for D-prefixed destination specifiers (DBOTH and DSTDOUT). When encountered, the system evaluates the state of _debug. If the pipeline is not running with debug flags enabled, dest is re-routed strictly to "LOG", which silences terminal output while guaranteeing that diagnostic records remain intact within the physical log file. If _debug is enabled, the leading character is stripped (dest = dest[1:]), allowing the message to print to the console while preserving its original severity color mapping defined in COLORS.

docs.title: emit_raw()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def emit_raw(level: str, text: str, dest: str = "BOTH") -> None:

Description: Dispatches unmanaged, dynamic, or structurally arbitrary text to the console and/or logger using explicit severity styling. Unlike emit(), this function does not perform lookups against strings.csv and does not apply {placeholder} substitutions. It is designed for variable multi-line payloads, AST crawl summaries, progress bars, and transient tabular diagnostics.

Parameters: * level (str): The severity level string governing ANSI color codes and Python logging priorities (e.g., "PROGRESS", "SUCCESS", "WARNING", "ERROR", "INFO", "DEBUG", "FILE_WRITE"). * text (str): The fully formatted string content to emit. * dest (str): Target destination stream. Accepts "BOTH", "STDOUT", or "LOG". Defaults to "BOTH".

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised. Unmapped severity strings fall back to plain uncolored text and default logging.INFO priority.

Example: 

# Emitting ad-hoc status information
emit_raw("WARNING", "Custom warning message regarding external API rate limits")
emit_raw("DEBUG", "Skipping binary file during AST walk", dest="LOG")

The implementation controls ad-hoc console printing and logger dispatch:

def emit_raw(level, text, dest="BOTH"):
    """Emit a pre-formatted string with explicit level styling.

    Use for dynamic/structural output that doesn't come from strings.csv
    (e.g., numbered file lists, batch details, crawl summary tables).
    """
    # DEBUG-level: suppress console unless --debug is active
    if level == "DEBUG" and not _debug:
        dest = "LOG"

    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _logger.log(LOG_LEVELS.get(level, logging.INFO), text)

emit_raw() enforces an implicit debug gate when level == "DEBUG". Even if a caller specifies dest="BOTH" or dest="STDOUT", the destination is mutated to "LOG" unless _debug evaluates to True. This prevents verbose crawl traces, chunk distributions, and sub-tree skips from polluting standard execution views while retaining complete fidelity within diagnostic trace files.

docs.title: get()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get(key: str, **kwargs: object) -> str:

Description: Retrieves a translated string template directly from the in-memory cache, executes variable substitution using provided keyword arguments, and returns the resulting string without emitting anything to terminal streams or log files. This function is designed for generating Markdown content, document headers, navigation labels, and UI strings managed by utils/mkdocs.py.

Parameters: * key (str): The target identifier corresponding to a STRING_KEY in strings.csv. * **kwargs (object): Values mapped to substitution placeholders present within the target string.

Returns: * str: The localized, substituted string. If the key is not present in the registry, the function falls back to returning the key string directly.

Raises: * No exceptions raised. Template interpolation errors are suppressed by _format_safe().

Example: 

# Retrieving UI headers for documentation landing pages
tutorial_header = get("UI_TUTORIAL")
index_title = get("UI_INDEX_TITLE", project="Codebase-Knowledge-Builder")

The implementation resolves the raw template from memory:

def get(key, **kwargs):
    """Get a translated string without printing or logging.

    Use for UI strings embedded in generated markdown (index.md headings, etc.).
    Returns the raw translated text with variable substitution applied.
    """
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        return key  # Fallback: return the key itself
    return _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)

The return fallback mechanism ensures downstream document generation nodes never encounter NoneType errors or empty strings when an unexpected translation key is referenced. By returning key verbatim upon lookup misses, the system allows missing configuration references to remain visible directly in generated documentation markdown as obvious diagnostic placeholders.

docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name: str = "project", mode: str = "tutorial") -> str:

Description: Configures dedicated file-based logging for the running process instance. It resolves the output directory (respecting the LOG_DIR environment variable), sanitizes project and execution mode names to eliminate illegal filesystem characters, constructs a unique timestamped filename, flushes existing handlers on _logger, binds a new logging.FileHandler using UTF-8 encoding, and writes initial execution metadata blocks.

Parameters: * project_name (str): The name of the target repository or codebase under analysis. Defaults to "project". * mode (str): The current pipeline execution mode (e.g., "tutorial", "api-reference", "quickstart"). Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: The absolute or normalized filesystem path of the initialized log file.

Raises: * OSError: If the log directory cannot be created due to filesystem permissions.

Example: 

# Initializing run logging from CLI arguments
log_path = configure_logging(project_name="my-org/backend-api", mode="api-reference")
# Resulting log file: logs/my_org_backend_api_api_reference_20250520_143000.log

The implementation performs path generation, handler registration, and header output:

def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    """Configure file-based logging for this run.

    Creates a new log file per invocation:
        logs/{project_name}_{mode}_{YYYYMMDD_HHmmss}.log

    Must be called from main() after parsing CLI arguments.
    """
    from datetime import datetime

    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_file = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Remove any existing handlers (e.g., NullHandler) and add the file handler
    _logger.handlers.clear()
    file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_file, encoding="utf-8")
    file_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"))
    _logger.addHandler(file_handler)

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    _logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    _logger.info(f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}")
    _logger.info(f"Log file: {log_file}")
    _logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")

    return log_file

Filename sanitization is enforced via a character whitelist: c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_". This protects Unix and Windows filesystems against invalid characters when repository identifiers contain forward slashes, spaces, or protocol prefixes (e.g., git@github.com:owner/repo.git). By calling _logger.handlers.clear(), the function prevents duplicate log lines from accumulating across iterative unit test invocations or multiple orchestrator runs within the same Python process.

docs.title: _format_safe()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _format_safe(template: str, kwargs: dict) -> str:

Description: Executes string interpolation using Python's standard str.format(**kwargs) protocol while defensively intercepting formatting exceptions. If placeholders within template fail to resolve against keys in kwargs, or if indices are malformed, the raw unformatted template is returned without raising an exception.

Parameters: * template (str): The source format string containing {placeholder} variables. * kwargs (dict): The mapping of keyword arguments intended for interpolation.

Returns: * str: The successfully interpolated string, or the unaltered template if an interpolation error occurs.

Raises: * No exceptions raised internally (KeyError, IndexError, and ValueError are intercepted).

Example: 

# Internal call site from emit()
text = _format_safe("Processing chapter {chapter_num}: {name}", {"chapter_num": 1, "name": "Architecture"})
# Fallback on missing keys
fallback_text = _format_safe("Processing chapter {chapter_num}: {name}", {"chapter_num": 1})
# Returns: "Processing chapter {chapter_num}: {name}"

The underlying implementation relies on a basic guarded block:

def _format_safe(template, kwargs):
    """Apply .format(**kwargs) with graceful fallback on missing keys."""
    try:
        return template.format(**kwargs)
    except (KeyError, IndexError, ValueError):
        return template

This helper insulates the application from crashes caused by mismatched placeholder syntax in dynamic LLM-generated translation outputs. If an external model inadvertently translates or drops a variable placeholder (e.g., changing {chapter_num} to {so_chuong}), subsequent emit() operations safely degrade to emitting the raw text rather than terminating pipeline execution with an unhandled KeyError.

docs.title: _load_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _load_strings() -> None:

Description: Parses strings.csv from disk and populates the module's private _strings registry. It parses CSV headers using csv.DictReader configured with utf-8-sig encoding to handle UTF-8 Byte Order Marks (BOM). For every row, it extracts the key, output styling level, dispatch destination, and target language text. If the target language column does not exist or contains an empty string, it falls back to reading the english column.

Parameters: * None. Operates directly on the module-level state variables _csv_path, _lang_col, _language, and _strings.

Returns: * None

Raises: * OSError: If the file path points to an unreadable device, though the function verifies os.path.exists(_csv_path) prior to opening.

Example: 

# Executed within init() or after _write_translations_to_csv()
_load_strings()

The file loading loop processes the CSV records into memory:

def _load_strings():
    """Load all strings from strings.csv."""
    global _strings
    _strings = {}

    if not _csv_path or not os.path.exists(_csv_path):
        return

    translated_count = 0
    total_count = 0

    with open(_csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key.startswith("#"):
                continue

            level = row.get("LEVEL", "INFO").strip()
            dest = row.get("DEST", "BOTH").strip()

            # Priority: language column → English fallback
            text = row.get(_lang_col, "").strip()
            if text:
                translated_count += 1
            else:
                text = row.get("english", "").strip()

            total_count += 1
            _strings[key] = {"text": text, "level": level, "dest": dest}

    if _lang_col != "english" and translated_count == total_count:
        emit_raw("SUCCESS", f"[i18n] {_language} — loaded {translated_count} strings from CSV")

The parser ignores empty lines and comments (key.startswith("#")). It tallies translation completeness via translated_count against total_count. If a non-English language is fully localized, it issues an immediate SUCCESS confirmation banner via emit_raw().

docs.title: _auto_translate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _auto_translate() -> None:

Description: Performs dynamic, batch runtime translation for any strings lacking translations in the active target language column. It inspects the CSV file to compile an inventory of missing keys, constructs a structured prompt referencing prompts/common/translate_strings.md, dispatches the request to utils/call_llm.py, extracts the resulting JSON dictionary via regular expressions, persists the new translations back into strings.csv, and reloads the in-memory string registry.

Parameters: * None. Reads _lang_col, _language, _csv_path, _use_cache, and _thinking_level.

Returns: * None

Raises: * Catches all exceptions internally (Exception), logging a warning and falling back to English.

docs.title: Phase 1: Missing Strings Discovery
docs.text:
The function scans strings.csv to identify whether the target language column exists and aggregates missing entries:

    if _lang_col == "english":
        return

    if not _csv_path or not os.path.exists(_csv_path):
        return

    # Collect strings that have no translation in the target language column
    missing = {}
    is_new_column = False
    with open(_csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        fieldnames = list(reader.fieldnames)
        is_new_column = _lang_col not in fieldnames
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key.startswith("#"):
                continue
            # Check if the language column exists and has a value
            lang_text = row.get(_lang_col, "").strip() if _lang_col in fieldnames else ""
            if lang_text:
                continue  # Already translated

            english_text = row.get("english", "").strip()
            if english_text:
                missing[key] = english_text

    if not missing:
        return

During discovery, the function evaluates reader.fieldnames against _lang_col. If the language has never been used before, is_new_column evaluates to True. The crawler aggregates all non-empty english entries corresponding to unpopulated target language cells into a missing dictionary keyed by STRING_KEY.

docs.title: Phase 2: LLM Translation Dispatch and Parsing
docs.text:
The system loads the translation prompt template, formats the payload as JSON, and invokes the inference provider:

    # Report what we found
    if is_new_column:
        emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] New language '{_language}' — adding column to strings.csv")
    emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] {len(missing)} strings need translation to {_language}")

    # Batch translate via LLM
    try:
        from utils.call_llm import call_llm

        entries_json = json.dumps(missing, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

        # Load prompt template from prompts/common/translate_strings.md
        prompt_path = os.path.join(
            os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
            "prompts",
            "common",
            "translate_strings.md",
        )
        with open(prompt_path, encoding="utf-8") as pf:
            prompt_template = pf.read()
        prompt = prompt_template.format(language=_language, entries=entries_json)

        emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] Calling LLM to translate {len(missing)} strings...")
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=_use_cache, thinking_level=_thinking_level)

        # Extract JSON from response
        json_match = re.search(r"\{[^{}]*(?:\{[^{}]*\}[^{}]*)*\}", response, re.DOTALL)
        if json_match:
            translations = json.loads(json_match.group())
            translated_count = len(translations)

            # Write translations back into strings.csv
            _write_translations_to_csv(translations)
            emit_raw("SUCCESS", f"[i18n] Translated {translated_count}/{len(missing)} strings — saved to strings.csv")

            # Reload strings from the updated CSV so all translations are active
            _load_strings()
        else:
            emit_raw("WARNING", "[i18n] LLM response did not contain valid JSON — falling back to English")

    except Exception as e:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"[i18n] Translation failed: {e} — falling back to English")

The LLM query uses call_llm() imported dynamically from utils/call_llm.py to avoid circular import dependencies at module load time. The prompt template instructs the model to return a strict JSON dictionary mapping each STRING_KEY to its translated equivalent while keeping format placeholders intact. A nested regular expression (r"\{[^{}]*(?:\{[^{}]*\}[^{}]*)*\}") extracts the JSON block even if the model prefixes or suffixes its response with Markdown fences or explanatory text.

docs.title: _write_translations_to_csv()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _write_translations_to_csv(translations: dict[str, str]) -> None:

Description: Persists newly translated key-value pairs back into strings.csv. If the target language column does not already exist in the CSV header, it appends the new column. It reads all existing rows, mutates rows matching keys present in translations, and rewrites the entire file using utf-8-sig encoding with newline="" to ensure consistent formatting across operating systems and Excel environments.

Parameters: * translations (dict[str, str]): A dictionary mapping STRING_KEY strings to their corresponding localized translations.

Returns: * None

Raises: * OSError: If write permissions are restricted on the target CSV file.

Example: 

# Internal invocation from _auto_translate()
_write_translations_to_csv({
    "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER": "Đang gọi LLM để viết chương {chapter_num}: {name}...",
    "UI_TUTORIAL": "Hướng dẫn chi tiết"
})

The file mutation pattern handles column updates and row persistence:

def _write_translations_to_csv(translations):
    """Write LLM translations back into strings.csv, persisting them for future runs.

    If the target language column doesn't exist, it is added to the CSV.
    """
    rows = []
    fieldnames = None

    with open(_csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        fieldnames = list(reader.fieldnames)
        # Add language column if it doesn't exist
        if _lang_col not in fieldnames:
            fieldnames.append(_lang_col)
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if key in translations:
                row[_lang_col] = translations[key]
            rows.append(row)

    # Write with BOM so Excel opens as UTF-8 without extra import steps
    with open(_csv_path, "w", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)

The CSV rewrite process updates the file atomically by reading all rows into memory, applying translation updates to matching keys, and writing the full dataset back out. Opening with utf-8-sig ensures that modern spreadsheet editors like Microsoft Excel automatically detect UTF-8 encoding without requiring manual CSV import wizard steps.

docs.title: strings.csv Record Schema
docs.text:
The persistent localization registry stored at utils/strings.csv follows a tabular schema where each record defines a discrete user-facing message, its visual severity styling, its stream routing rules, and localized text across supported languages.

Field Type Description Example Values STRING_KEY str Unique primary key identifying the message across code call sites. Lines starting with # are treated as comments. "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER", "UI_TUTORIAL" LEVEL str Severity classification mapping to ANSI terminal escape colors and Python logging priorities. "PROGRESS", "SUCCESS", "WARNING", "ERROR", "INFO", "DEBUG", "FILE_WRITE" DEST str Output destination policy controlling routing to standard output, file logging, or both. "BOTH", "STDOUT", "LOG", "DBOTH", "DSTDOUT" english str Baseline English text template containing optional {placeholder} tokens for interpolation. "Generating chapter {chapter_num}: {name}..." <lang_col> str Dynamic column added per target language containing localized translation templates. "Đang tạo chương {chapter_num}: {name}..."

docs.title: In-Memory String Registry Cache (_strings)
docs.text:
The private module-level dictionary _strings holds normalized message configurations parsed from strings.csv during _load_strings().

Field Type Description text str The localized format template string (falling back to English if untranslated). level str Severity level string used to resolve colors from COLORS and logging priorities from LOG_LEVELS. dest str Output destination flag ("BOTH", "STDOUT", "LOG", "DBOTH", "DSTDOUT"). 
# Internal shape of _strings entry
{
    "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER": {
        "text": "Writing chapter {chapter_num}: {name}...",
        "level": "PROGRESS",
        "dest": "BOTH"
    }
}

docs.title: Color Palette Mapping (COLORS)
docs.text:
The module defines a static mapping between logical severity levels and ANSI color escape sequences.

Level Identifier ANSI Sequence Display Appearance Intended Operational Semantics "PROGRESS" \033[96m Cyan Active LLM queries, multi-file crawl batches, phase milestones. "SUCCESS" \033[92m Green Task completions, cache hits, successful artifact writes. "WARNING" \033[93m Yellow Token budget alerts, fallback triggers, rate limit warnings. "ERROR" \033[91m Red Pipeline failures, unrecoverable API errors, fatal terminations. "INFO" "" Standard Terminal Text Informational labels, configuration values, run metadata. "DEBUG" \033[90m Dark Gray Skipped files, raw AST metrics, detailed execution traces. "FILE_WRITE" "" Standard Terminal Text Indented file write notices (" - Wrote {path}"). "UI" "" N/A Reserved for Markdown artifacts; never directly printed to console.

docs.title: Python Logging Severity Mapping (LOG_LEVELS)
docs.text:
Translates application-level severity specifiers to standard library logging priorities:

Level Identifier Python Logger Level Value "PROGRESS" logging.INFO 20 "SUCCESS" logging.INFO 20 "WARNING" logging.WARNING 30 "ERROR" logging.ERROR 40 "INFO" logging.INFO 20 "DEBUG" logging.DEBUG 10 "FILE_WRITE" logging.DEBUG 10

docs.title: Destination Routing Codes (DEST)
docs.text:
The DEST column in strings.csv and the dest parameter in emit_raw() govern stream delivery:

Destination Code Terminal Output (sys.stdout) Disk Logger (logging.FileHandler) Gating Condition "BOTH" Yes (ANSI colored) Yes (Plain text) Always active. "STDOUT" Yes (ANSI colored) No Always active. "LOG" No Yes (Plain text) Always active. "DBOTH" Yes (ANSI colored) Yes (Plain text) Gated: Suppressed from stdout unless --debug is specified. Always logged. "DSTDOUT" Yes (ANSI colored) No Gated: Suppressed completely unless --debug is specified.

docs.title: Template Variable Substitution Failures
docs.text:
During template interpolation in _format_safe(), user-supplied arguments may fail to match placeholder tokens defined within strings.csv. This commonly occurs when an LLM auto-translation inadvertently alters placeholder syntax (e.g., modifying {count} to {total}). The helper intercepts KeyError, IndexError, and ValueError, returning the raw template string instead of throwing an exception:

try:
    return template.format(**kwargs)
except (KeyError, IndexError, ValueError):
    return template

docs.title: Missing Registry Key Lookups
docs.text:
When emit(key) encounters an unrecognized string key, it catches the lookup miss through dictionary inspection:

entry = _strings.get(key)
if not entry:
    print(f"[UNKNOWN STRING: {key}]")
    return

This ensures that typos in string keys do not cause fatal runtime crashes, while immediately exposing missing keys in the terminal output for developers to see.

docs.title: Automated Translation Fault Tolerance
docs.text:
Dynamic localization in _auto_translate() is wrapped in a broad exception handler:

try:
    # LLM translation dispatch, JSON parsing, and disk writes
    ...
except Exception as e:
    emit_raw("WARNING", f"[i18n] Translation failed: {e} — falling back to English")

If the network connection drops, API credentials fail, or the external model returns invalid JSON, the exception is intercepted. The system issues a WARNING and continues execution using baseline English strings, ensuring that localization issues never disrupt core documentation generation.

docs.title: prompts.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/prompts.py

Following the observability and localization mechanics established in output.py, the utils/prompts.py module defines the prompt loading, synthesis, and response parsing infrastructure for the documentation generation pipeline. It coordinates the creation of targeted system instructions for Large Language Models (LLMs) and isolates the deserialization logic required to process structured outputs returned by inference gateways.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/prompts.py acts as the prompt engineering and structured-output decoding layer of the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder architecture. In an automated documentation pipeline, execution nodes frequently require specialized instructions conditioned on project metadata, file paths, and target output languages. Simultaneously, intermediate pipeline states depend on structured data (such as lists of code file indices or navigation hierarchies) extracted reliably from non-deterministic LLM text responses. This module bridges prompt assembly and response processing, decoupling orchestration nodes in nodes.py from raw string templating and Markdown extraction logic.

The module operates across two functional domains: 1. Prompt Ingestion and Construction: File-based prompt templates residing in the filesystem tree under prompts/ are located and ingested via load_prompt_template(). The module supports mode-driven directory scoping (tutorial, advanced, or arbitrary mode identifiers). For specialized pipeline stages where disk-based templates are inappropriate, the module provides dynamic string synthesis functions—namely build_code_file_filter_prompt() for identifying executable code modules, and build_chapter_summary_prompt() for compiling multi-dimensional technical chapter abstracts used for cross-chapter context injection. 2. Structured Response Extraction: Because LLMs return freeform conversational strings interspersed with Markdown formatting, parse_yaml_response() extracts text contained within ```yaml code fences and deserializes it into native Python dictionaries or lists via PyYAML.

flowchart TD

        initLoad["load_prompt_template()"]
        dirBranch{"Mode Explicitly Defined?"}

        tutDir["Use 'tutorial' directory"]
        readFS["Read file from disk via utf-8-sig"]

    end

    subgraph PromptBuilders["Dynamic Prompt Synthesis"]
        filterPrompt["build_code_file_filter_prompt()"]
        summaryPrompt["build_chapter_summary_prompt()"]
    end

    subgraph ResponseParsing["Structured Output Parsing"]
        parseYaml["parse_yaml_response()"]
        splitFence["Isolate content between ```yaml and ```"]
        yamlSafe["yaml.safe_load()"]
        errCatch{"Parsing or Extraction Failed?"}
        raiseErr["Raise ValueError"]

    end

    dirBranch -- Yes --> customDir
    dirBranch -- No --> modeBranch
    modeBranch -- Yes --> advDir
    modeBranch -- No --> tutDir

The architecture addresses several operational considerations: * Path Resolution Autonomy: Template loading calculates root paths relative to __file__, allowing portable execution across development environments, container images, or working directories. * Encoding Resiliency: Disk reads enforce utf-8-sig encoding, stripping Byte Order Marks (BOM) transparently to prevent parsing syntax errors in downstream Jinja or Python formatting operations. * Decoupled Telemetry: The module uses late imports (from utils.output import emit_raw) inside load_prompt_template() to log template access directly to internal debug logs without triggering circular dependency loops during interpreter startup.

docs.title: load_prompt_template()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None) -> str

Description: Locates and loads the UTF-8 encoded text of a Markdown prompt template from the repository's prompts/ filesystem hierarchy. The target directory is dynamically resolved according to a three-tier precedence model: if mode is explicitly provided, it selects prompts/{mode}/; otherwise, if advanced_mode is True, it selects prompts/advanced/; defaulting finally to prompts/tutorial/.

Once the canonical path is computed relative to the project root, the file is read using utf-8-sig encoding. The method then issues a debug diagnostic to the operational log via a late import of emit_raw(), ensuring template access is recorded without polluting stdout.

docs.title: Phase 1: Directory Scope Resolution
docs.text:
if mode is None:
        prompt_dir = "advanced" if advanced_mode else "tutorial"
    else:
        prompt_dir = mode
This phase determines which subdirectory under prompts/ holds the requested template. By checking mode is None first, callers can pass arbitrary mode strings (such as "api-reference" or specialized testing profiles) directly. If mode is unspecified, the binary advanced_mode flag routes between "advanced" and "tutorial".

docs.title: Phase 2: Filesystem Resolution and Ingestion
docs.text:
path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "prompts", prompt_dir, f"{template_name}.md")
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        content = f.read()
The absolute path is determined by stepping up two directory levels from utils/prompts.py to reach the repository root, then descending into prompts/{prompt_dir}/{template_name}.md. File opening explicitly mandates utf-8-sig to gracefully strip Windows UTF-8 BOM headers that may be introduced during manual template editing.

docs.title: Phase 3: Telemetry Dispatch
docs.text:
from utils.output import emit_raw

    emit_raw("DEBUG", f"load_prompt_template | loaded '{template_name}.md' from prompts/{prompt_dir}/", dest="LOG")
    return content
The final phase lazily imports emit_raw from utils.output. This prevents module-level circular imports between output telemetry and prompt initialization. It logs the resolution event at severity level "DEBUG" explicitly directed to the "LOG" destination (bypassing standard output). The raw template string is then returned to the caller.

Parameters: * template_name (str): Base name of the prompt Markdown file (excluding the .md extension). * advanced_mode (bool, optional): Legacy boolean flag used when mode is None. Selects "advanced" if True, or "tutorial" if False. Defaults to False. * mode (str | None, optional): Explicit subdirectory name under prompts/ to load templates from. Overrides advanced_mode when provided. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The complete raw string content of the resolved template file.

Raises: * FileNotFoundError: If the constructed path does not exist on disk. * IOError: If the file cannot be accessed due to OS permissions.

Example: 

# Sourced from utils/prompts.py implementation:
path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "prompts", prompt_dir, f"{template_name}.md")
with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
    content = f.read()
from utils.output import emit_raw

emit_raw("DEBUG", f"load_prompt_template | loaded '{template_name}.md' from prompts/{prompt_dir}/", dest="LOG")

docs.title: parse_yaml_response()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_yaml_response(response: str) -> Any

Description: Isolates, sanitizes, and parses YAML data structures embedded within an LLM completion string. Standard generative language models frequently envelope structured responses in Markdown code blocks. parse_yaml_response() extracts text specifically bounded by ```yaml and closing ``` tokens, ignoring preamble explanations, thinking traces, or postscript commentary.

The extracted substring is then parsed via yaml.safe_load(). If the delimiters are missing or if the payload contains invalid YAML syntax, the routine intercepts the resulting standard exception and raises a formatted ValueError preserving the underlying cause.

docs.title: Phase 1: Boundary Isolation
docs.text:
try:
        yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0].strip()
The input string is stripped of leading and trailing whitespace, then partitioned using "```yaml" as the opening delimiter. Index 1 isolates the text immediately following the fence header. A subsequent partition on "```" selects index 0, extracting only the payload between the fences. A final .strip() removes boundary whitespace and carriage returns.

docs.title: Phase 2: Deserialization and Error Normalization
docs.text:
return yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e
The isolated YAML string is passed to yaml.safe_load(), which converts the text into corresponding native Python collections (e.g., list, dict, int, str). If an IndexError occurs during splitting (indicating missing code fences) or a yaml.YAMLError occurs during parsing, the exception is caught and re-raised as a standard ValueError with chained context (from e).

Parameters: * response (str): The raw text response received from an LLM call.

Returns: * Any: The deserialized Python data structure (typically a dict or list).

Raises: * ValueError: If "```yaml" or "```" fences are missing, or if the extracted payload violates YAML syntax rules.

Example: 

# Sourced from utils/prompts.py implementation:
try:
    yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0].strip()
    return yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
except Exception as e:
    raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e

docs.title: build_code_file_filter_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str

Description: Synthesizes the prompt payload utilized by file mapper stages (such as DeterministicFileMapper in API-reference documentation mode). This prompt directs an LLM to evaluate an enumerated listing of repository files and filter out non-code assets, configurations, UI layouts, and build artifacts.

The generated prompt injects the target project_name and the pre-formatted file_listing string. It articulates explicit negative filtering constraints (specifying extensions like .xaml, .storyboard, .html, .xml, .json, .manifest, .ini, .csproj, and .sln) and mandates that the model output only a YAML list containing integer indices of genuine code modules.

docs.title: Prompt Assembly Phase
docs.text:
return (
        f"For the project `{project_name}`, here is the list of all files in the codebase:

"
        f"{file_listing}

"
        f"Your task is to identify WHICH of these files are ACTUAL CODE files that contain "
        f"APIs, functions, classes, or core business logic.
"
        f"EXCLUDE: UI layouts (like .xaml, .storyboard, .html), configuration files "
        f"(like .xml, .json, .manifest, .ini), static assets, build scripts "
        f"(like .csproj, .sln), and documentation.

"
        f"Return ONLY a YAML list of the file indices that should be documented as code modules.

"
        f"```yaml
- 0
- 1
- 3
```"
    )
The prompt combines the contextual inputs into a single multiline string. By terminating the prompt with a concrete Markdown fence example (```yaml - 0 - 1 - 3 ```), the instruction anchors the expected few-shot schema pattern for zero-shot inference, ensuring compatibility with parse_yaml_response().

Parameters: * project_name (str): Name or identifier of the repository being processed. * file_listing (str): Enumerated list of repository files (typically formatted with index identifiers such as (idx:0) path/to/file.py via files.py).

Returns: * str: The fully interpolated prompt string ready for LLM consumption.

Example: 

# Direct implementation extracted from utils/prompts.py:
prompt = build_code_file_filter_prompt(
    project_name="Codebase-Knowledge-Builder",
    file_listing="(idx:0) utils/prompts.py
(idx:1) config.json
(idx:2) main.py"
)

docs.title: build_chapter_summary_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str

Description: Assembles the prompt required to synthesize a standardized, 4-dimension technical brief of a completed documentation chapter. This summary is injected into subsequent chapter synthesis prompts to maintain architectural coherence and cross-chapter referencing across large documentation jobs.

The prompt enforces a strict structure requiring 3 to 5 concise technical sentences across four architectural dimensions: 1. Component Scope & Responsibility: Core domain, problem space, and system role. 2. Key Technical Elements: Explicit naming and characterization of classes, services, functions, and protocols. 3. Implementation Patterns & Architecture: Design patterns, communication channels, error strategies, and threading models. 4. System Integration & Dependencies: External consumption, interface contracts, and boundary touchpoints.

If the requested language parameter is set to any value other than "english" (case-insensitive), an explicit language constraint prefix is dynamically prepended to ensure localized generation.

docs.title: Prompt Assembly Phase
docs.text:
lang_instruction = f"Write the entire summary in {language.capitalize()}. " if language.lower() != "english" else ""
    return (
        f"{lang_instruction}"
        f"Summarize the following documentation chapter as a structured technical brief. "
        f"For EACH of the 4 points below, write 3-5 concise technical sentences:\n\n"
        f"(1) **Component Scope & Responsibility**: What is the main technical domain this "
        f"chapter covers? What problems does it solve and what role does it play in the system?\n\n"
        f"(2) **Key Technical Elements**: What are the specific classes, services, functions, "
        f"data models, or protocols discussed? Name them and describe their concrete roles.\n\n"
        f"(3) **Implementation Patterns & Architecture**: What design patterns, communication "
        f"protocols, data flow strategies, error handling mechanisms, or security measures "
        f"are covered? How are they implemented?\n\n"
        f"(4) **System Integration & Dependencies**: How does this component interface with "
        f"other parts of the system? What does it consume from or provide to other components? "
        f"What are the key integration points?\n\n"
        f"---\n"
        f"Chapter {chapter_num}: {abstraction_name}\n"
        f"{chapter_content}"
    )
The function evaluates the target language and conditionally builds the lang_instruction string. It then formats the four technical questions, appending the chapter index, title, and body text separated by a Markdown thematic break (---).

Parameters: * chapter_num (int): Sequential index of the chapter being summarized. * abstraction_name (str): Title or high-level abstraction name representing the chapter. * chapter_content (str): Markdown text of the fully generated chapter. * language (str, optional): Target natural language for the summary output. Defaults to "english".

Returns: * str: The fully constructed technical summary prompt string.

Example: 

# Direct implementation extracted from utils/prompts.py:
prompt = build_chapter_summary_prompt(
    chapter_num=1,
    abstraction_name="LLM Execution Gateway",
    chapter_content="## Technical Overview\nThis module manages LLM routing...",
    language="english"
)

docs.title: Data Structures
docs.text: The module does not declare custom object classes; instead, it relies on structured string contracts and parsed deserialization schemas.

docs.title: Parsed YAML Extraction Schemas
docs.text: parse_yaml_response() transforms YAML fenced blocks into native Python data structures. The expected shapes depend on the consuming pipeline node:

docs.title: 1. Integer Index List Schema

Emitted by LLM responses answering build_code_file_filter_prompt():

Field Element Type Description [item] int Zero-based index of a valid code file corresponding to the indexed input listing.

Example Payload: 

- 0
- 1
- 3

Emitted by LLM clustering tasks (e.g., when structuring MkDocs navigation in mkdocs.py):

Field Name Type Description title str Display title of the documentation grouping or category. items list[str] List of file paths, module names, or sub-group mappings.

docs.title: Technical Summary Schema
docs.text:
build_chapter_summary_prompt() enforces a standardized output contract across four discrete technical dimensions:

Dimension Header Expected Content Format Functional Role in Pipeline (1) **Component Scope & Responsibility** 3–5 concise technical sentences Defines boundary scope and domain problems resolved. (2) **Key Technical Elements** 3–5 concise technical sentences Enumerates concrete functions, classes, and protocol entities. (3) **Implementation Patterns & Architecture** 3–5 concise technical sentences Summarizes algorithms, design patterns, and failure paths. (4) **System Integration & Dependencies** 3–5 concise technical sentences Details inbound/outbound calls, data shapes, and contracts.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: utils/prompts.py applies targeted defensive error management for file I/O and non-deterministic LLM output parsing:

docs.title: 1. Code Fence Partitioning and YAML Syntax Trapping
docs.text: Language models frequently generate conversational commentary alongside structured outputs. parse_yaml_response() isolates the block using .split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0]. * If the opening token "```yaml" or closing token "```" is missing, a Python IndexError is triggered during list indexing. * If the enclosed payload contains unescaped characters, inconsistent tab indentations, or invalid scalar mappings, yaml.safe_load() raises yaml.YAMLError (or one of its subclasses such as yaml.scanner.ScannerError or yaml.parser.ParserError). * All exceptions are caught uniformly by an except Exception as e: block and re-raised as a standard ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e. This consolidates diverse downstream parsing failures into a single predictable exception type that orchestration nodes in nodes.py can catch and handle (e.g., by triggering a retry prompt).

docs.title: 2. Filesystem Encoding and Path Anomalies
docs.text: In load_prompt_template(): * UTF-8 Byte Order Marks (BOM): Opening files with utf-8-sig prevents \ufeff prefix characters from remaining in the template string, avoiding subtle formatting errors during subsequent string interpolation. * Missing Templates: If a referenced template_name does not exist within prompts/{prompt_dir}/, the native FileNotFoundError propagates directly to the calling node, signaling a misconfigured pipeline stage.

docs.title: token_utils.py
docs.text: Source: utils/token_utils.py

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
Following the prompt management and structured decoding mechanics documented in utils/prompts.py, the utils/token_utils.py module provides token budgeting, context window resolution, and execution telemetry for the pipeline. In Large Language Model (LLM) documentation pipelines, unbounded prompt assembly risks exceeding provider context windows, resulting in costly HTTP 400 errors, silent payload truncation, or mid-generation failures. This module establishes a unified metering and budgeting layer that operates upstream of the execution gateway documented in utils/call_llm.py.

The component operates as a standalone utility service designed around three core functions: lazy-loaded Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenization, dynamic context capacity resolution, and structured multi-channel telemetry emission. It wraps OpenAI's cl100k_base BPE tokenizer through the tiktoken library, providing a fallback mechanism that approximates token counts using character-length heuristics (len(text) // 4) when binary wheels or encoding assets fail to load. In addition to measuring strings, the module determines active model context boundaries by inspecting execution runtimes or querying external provider metadata endpoints.

Telemetry tracking is integrated through a dual-channel reporting mechanism. When execution nodes in nodes.py construct prompts, token_utils.py measures prompt size against model thresholds and breaks down composite prompts (such as system instructions, file contents, and dependency graphs) into per-component allocations. It routes human-readable summaries to the terminal using localized string emission in utils/output.py, while appending structured single-line execution records to the shared persistent log file.
